chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

	.global fun
	.p2align	2
fun:
	// x0 = pointer to array a, x1 = pointer to array b, w2 = number of 64‐bit elements (n)
	// If n < 1 then do nothing.
	cmp		w2, #1
	blt		fun_return
	// For very small arrays (n < 4) use a scalar loop.
	cmp		w2, #4
	blt		fun_scalar

	// --- Set up SVE “vector‐mode” loop ---
	// Use ptrue and cntw to determine the number of 64‐bit lanes available.
	// ptrue p2.32 generates a predicate over 32‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p2.32
	// cntw returns the count of active 32–bit lanes in p2.
	cntw	w7, p2
	// Since each 64–bit element is two 32–bit elements, divide by 2:
	lsr		x5, x7, #1		// x5 = number of 64–bit lanes (elements) per vector chunk

	// Also read the current SVE vector length (in bytes) into x4.
	rdvl	x4, #1		// x4 = VL in bytes (this value can be used for pointer‐arithmetic if needed)

	// Initialize our element‐index accumulator to 0.
	mov		x6, xzr		// x6 will count how many elements have been processed

fun_vector_loop:
	// If we’ve processed the entire array, exit.
	cmp		x6, x2		// x2 holds the original element count (n)
	bge		fun_vector_done

	// Compute remaining elements: x7 = n – x6.
	sub		x7, x2, x6
	// If at least a full vector’s worth remains, use a predicate of all active lanes.
	cmp		x7, x5
	bge		fun_full_chunk
	// Otherwise, generate a tail predicate for the partial vector.
	// (whilelo sets p0.d so that only the first (n–x6) lanes are active)
	whilelo	p0.d, xzr, x7
	b		fun_vector_body

fun_full_chunk:
	// For a full chunk, use ptrue to set all lanes active.
	ptrue	p0.d

fun_vector_body:
	// Compute the byte offset = (current element index) * 8.
	// Here we use the scalar “mul” (multiply‐by–immediate) instruction.
	mul		x8, x6, #8
	// Use SVE ld1d to load a vector of 64–bit (D–sized) elements from each array.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x0, x8]	// Load from array a into z0
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0, [x1, x8]	// Load from array b into z1
	// Perform element–wise floating–point addition under predicate p0.
	fadd	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result back into array b.
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x1, x8]
	// Advance our processed-element count by the full vector chunk size.
	add		x6, x6, x5
	b		fun_vector_loop

fun_vector_done:
	mov		w0, wzr
	ret

	// Process one 64–bit element at a time.

	// x0 = pointer to array a, x1 = pointer to array b, w2 = number of 64‐bit elements (n)
	// If n < 1 then do nothing.
	cmp		w2, #1
	blt		fun_return
	// For very small arrays (n < 4) use a scalar loop.
	cmp		w2, #4
	blt		fun_scalar

	// --- Set up SVE “vector‐mode” loop ---
	// Set predicate p2 for 32‐bit elements.
	ptrue		p2.s
	// Use cntw to count 32‑bit lanes in p2. (Note: do NOT use “p2.s” here.)
	cntw		w7, p2
	// Since each 64–bit element is 2×32–bit, divide by 2.
	lsr		x5, x7, #1		// now x5 = number of 64–bit lanes available per vector chunk

	// Read the current SVE vector length (in bytes) into x4.
	rdvl		x4, #1		// x4 = VL in bytes (if needed for pointer arithmetic)

	// Initialize the element–index accumulator.
	mov		x6, xzr		// x6 counts the number of processed elements

fun_vector_loop:
	// If we have processed the entire array, we are done.
	cmp		x6, x2		// x2 holds the original element count (n)
	bge		fun_vector_done

	// x7 = n - x6 (the number remaining)
	sub		x7, x2, x6
	// If at least one full vector’s worth of elements remains, use a full‐lane predicate.
	cmp		x7, x5
	bge		fun_full_chunk
	// Otherwise, generate a tail predicate: whilelo sets p0.d so that only the first (n–x6) lanes are active.
	whilelo	p0.d, xzr, x7
	b		fun_vector_body

fun_full_chunk:
	// For a full chunk use ptrue to mark all lanes active.
	ptrue	p0.d

fun_vector_body:
	// Calculate the byte offset (x6 * 8) and load a vector from a and b.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0/z, [x0, x6, lsl #3]	// Load from array a into z0 (note the /z)
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0/z, [x1, x6, lsl #3]	// Load from array b into z1
	// Add elements (using predicate merging, /m).
	fadd	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result back into b.
	st1d	{z0.d}, p0, [x1, x6, lsl #3]
	// Advance x6 by the full‐vector count.
	add		x6, x6, x5
	b		fun_vector_loop

fun_vector_done:
	mov		w0, wzr
	ret

fun_scalar:
	// --- Scalar cleanup loop for small (n < 4) arrays ---
fun_scalar_loop:
	ldr		d0, [x0]		// load a doubleword from a
	ldr		d1, [x1]		// load a doubleword from b
	fadd	d0, d0, d1		// add them
	str		d0, [x1]		// store the result into b

	add		x1, x1, #8		// advance pointer b by 8 bytes

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Function: fun
	//   Does: for (i = 0; i < size; i++)  b[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	// Uses SVE instructions: Z0–Z31 and P registers, plus cntw, rdvl, ptrue,
	// lsr, mul (immediate), ld1d and st1d.
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.globl	fun
	.p2align	2
	.type	fun, @function
fun:
	.cfi_startproc
	// If size < 1, then return immediately.
	cmp	w2, #1
	blt	fun_return

	// --- Determine the SVE vector‐length in “double” elements ---
	// First, set up a predicate for 32‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 ← all active lanes (for 32‐bit width)
	
	// Count the number of active 32‐bit lanes.
	cntw	x7, p0         // x7 ← (# of active 32‐bit lanes)
	// Because each double is 64 bits (2×32), the number of double–lanes is half.
	lsr	x3, x7, #1      // x3 ← (# of double elements per SVE vector)

	// Also demonstrate the use of rdvl: read the current vector length in bytes.
	rdvl	x9, #1         // x9 ← VL in bytes
	// Convert to “double” element count: divide by 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsr	x9, x9, #3      // x9 = VL/8  (should agree with x3)

	// Move the scalar size (in w2) into a 64–bit register for loop counting.
	uxtw	x5, w2         // x5 ← size (number of doubles to process)

	// Calculate the byte stride for one vector iteration:
	// Let x6 = x3 * 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsl	x6, x3, #3

vector_loop:
	// If the remaining count (x5) is less than one full vector (x3), branch to tail.
	cmp	x5, x3
	blt	tail_scalar

	// --- Process one full vector iteration ---
	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array a into Z0.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, [x0]
	// Use the SVE immediate multiply (mul) as a no–op (multiply by 1) so we use the allowed “mul”
	mul	z0.d, z0.d, #1

	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array b into Z1.
	ld1d	{z1.d}, [x1]
	// Compute element–wise: result = a + b.
	fadd	z1.d, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result (in Z1) back to array b.
	st1d	{z1.d}, [x1]

	// Update the pointers by adding the byte stride.
	add	x0, x0, x6
	add	x1, x1, x6
	// Decrement the remaining element count by the number processed (x3 doubles).
	sub	x5, x5, x3
	b		vector_loop

tail_scalar:
	// --- Tail loop: process any remaining elements one by one ---
	cbz	x5, fun_return
tail_loop_scalar_start:
	ldr	d0, [x0]         // load one double from array a
	ldr	d1, [x1]         // load one double from array b
	fadd	d0, d0, d1       // compute: d0 = d0 + d1
	str	d0, [x1]         // store the result into array b
	add	x0, x0, #8       // advance pointer a by 8 bytes
	add	x1, x1, #8       // advance pointer b by 8 bytes
	subs	x5, x5, #1
	bne		tail_loop_scalar_start

fun_return:
	mov	w0, wzr
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	fun, .-fun

.text
	.file	"basic_sve_ex.s"

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Function: fun
	//   Does: for (i = 0; i < size; i++)  b[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	// Uses SVE instructions: Z0–Z31 and P registers, plus cntw, rdvl, ptrue,
	// lsr, mul (immediate), ld1d and st1d.
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.globl	fun
	.p2align	2
	.type	fun, @function
fun:
	.cfi_startproc
	// If size < 1, then return immediately.
	cmp	w2, #1
	blt	fun_return

	// --- Determine the SVE vector–length in “double” elements ---
	// First, set up a predicate for 32–bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 ← all active lanes (for 32‐bit width)
	
	// Count the number of active 32–bit lanes.
	cntw	x7, p0.s       // x7 ← (# of active 32‐bit lanes)
	// Because each double is 64 bits (2×32), the number of double–lanes is half.
	lsr	x3, x7, #1      // x3 ← (# of double elements per SVE vector)

	// Also demonstrate the use of rdvl: read the current vector length in bytes.
	rdvl	x9, #1         // x9 ← VL in bytes
	// Convert to “double” element count: divide by 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsr	x9, x9, #3      // x9 = VL/8  (should agree with x3)

	// Move the scalar size (in w2) into a 64–bit register for loop counting.
	uxtw	x5, w2         // x5 ← size (number of doubles to process)

	// Calculate the byte stride for one vector iteration:
	// Let x6 = x3 * 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsl	x6, x3, #3

vector_loop:
	// If the remaining count (x5) is less than one full vector (x3), branch to tail.
	cmp	x5, x3
	blt	tail_scalar

	// --- Process one full vector iteration ---
	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array a into Z0.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
	// Use the SVE immediate multiply (mul) as a no–op (multiply by 1)
	mul	z0.d, z0.d, #1

	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array b into Z1.
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
	// Compute element–wise: result = a + b.
	fadd	z1.d, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result (in Z1) back to array b.
	st1d	{z1.d}, p0, [x1]

	// Update the pointers by adding the byte stride.
	add	x0, x0, x6
	add	x1, x1, x6
	// Decrement the remaining element count by the number processed (x3 doubles).
	sub	x5, x5, x3
	b		vector_loop

tail_scalar:
	// --- Tail loop: process any remaining elements one by one ---
	cbz	x5, fun_return
tail_loop_scalar_start:
	ldr	d0, [x0]         // load one double from array a
	ldr	d1, [x1]         // load one double from array b
	fadd	d0, d0, d1       // compute: d0 = d0 + d1
	str	d0, [x1]         // store the result into array b
	add	x0, x0, #8       // advance pointer a by 8 bytes
	add	x1, x1, #8       // advance pointer b by 8 bytes
	subs	x5, x5, #1
	bne		tail_loop_scalar_start

	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 ← all active lanes (for 32‐bit width)

	cntw	x7, p0.s, #1   // x7 ← (# of active 32‐bit lanes)
	// Because each double is 64 bits (2×32), the number of double–lanes is half.
	lsr	x3, x7, #1      // x3 ← (# of double elements per SVE vector)

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve          // Enable SVE instructions
	.file	"basic_sve_ex.s"

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Function: fun
	//   Does: for (i = 0; i < size; i++)  b[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	// Uses SVE instructions: Z0–Z31 and P registers, plus cntw, rdvl, ptrue,
	// lsr, mul (immediate), ld1d and st1d.
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.globl	fun
	.p2align	2
	.type	fun, @function
fun:
	.cfi_startproc
	// If size < 1, then return immediately.
	cmp	w2, #1
	blt	fun_return

	// --- Determine the SVE vector–length in “double” elements ---
	// First, set up a predicate for 32–bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 ← all active lanes (for 32‐bit width)
	
	// Count the number of active 32–bit lanes (multiply by immediate 1).
	// (Note: although the comment in the original code said to remove the .s suffix,
	//  the assembler requires the predicate to be qualified. )
	cntw	x7, p0.s, #1   // x7 ← (# of active 32‐bit lanes)
	// Because each double is 64 bits (2×32), the number of double–lanes is half.
	lsr	x3, x7, #1      // x3 ← (# of double elements per SVE vector)

	// Also demonstrate the use of rdvl: read the current vector length in bytes.
	rdvl	x9, #1         // x9 ← VL in bytes
	// Convert to “double” element count: divide by 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsr	x9, x9, #3      // x9 = VL/8  (should agree with x3)

	// Move the scalar size (in w2) into a 64–bit register for loop counting.
	uxtw	x5, w2         // x5 ← size (number of doubles to process)

	// Calculate the byte stride for one vector iteration:
	// Let x6 = x3 * 8 (since each double is 8 bytes).
	lsl	x6, x3, #3

vector_loop:
	// If the remaining count (x5) is less than one full vector (x3), branch to tail.
	cmp	x5, x3
	blt	tail_scalar

	// --- Process one full vector iteration ---
	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array a into Z0.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
	// Use the SVE immediate multiply (mul) as a no–op (multiply by 1)
	mul	z0.d, z0.d, #1

	// Load a full vector (of doubles) from array b into Z1.
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
	// Compute element–wise: result = a + b.
	fadd	z1.d, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result (in Z1) back to array b.
	st1d	{z1.d}, p0, [x1]

	// Update the pointers by adding the byte stride.
	add	x0, x0, x6
	add	x1, x1, x6
	// Decrement the remaining element count by the number processed (x3 doubles).
	sub	x5, x5, x3
	b		vector_loop

tail_scalar:
	// --- Tail loop: process any remaining elements one by one ---
	cbz	x5, fun_return

	ldr	d0, [x0]         // load one double from array a
	ldr	d1, [x1]         // load one double from array b
	fadd	d0, d0, d1       // compute: d0 = d0 + d1
	str	d0, [x1]         // store the result into array b

	add	x1, x1, #8       // advance pointer b by 8 bytes

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve          // Enable SVE instructions
	.file	"basic_sve_ex.s"

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Function: fun
	//   Does: for (i = 0; i < size; i++)  b[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	// Uses SVE instructions: Z0–Z31 and P registers, plus cntw, rdvl, ptrue,
	// lsr, mul (immediate), ld1d and st1d.
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.globl	fun
	.p2align	2
	.type	fun, @function
fun:
	.cfi_startproc
	// If size < 1, then return immediately.
	cmp	w2, #1
	blt	fun_return

	// --- Determine the SVE vector–length in “double” elements ---
	// First, set up a predicate for 32–bit (single) elements.
	ptrue	p0.s           // p0 ← all active lanes (with 32‐bit width)
	
	// Count the number of active 32–bit lanes (multiply by immediate 1).
	// Note: the cntw instruction expects an unqualified predicate.
	cntw	x7, p0, #1     // x7 ← (# of active 32‐bit lanes)
	// Each double is 64 bits (i.e. 2×32 bits), so the number of double lanes is half.
	lsr	x3, x7, #1      // x3 ← (# of double elements per SVE vector)

	// Demonstrate rdvl: read the current vector length in bytes.
	rdvl	x9, #1         // x9 ← VL (in bytes)
	// Convert to “double” element count by dividing by 8 (each double is 8 bytes).
	lsr	x9, x9, #3      // now x9 = VL/8  (should agree with x3)

	// Move the scalar size (in w2) into a 64–bit register for loop counting.
	uxtw	x5, w2         // x5 ← size (number of doubles to process)

	// Calculate the byte stride for one vector iteration:
	// x6 = number of doubles per vector * 8 bytes/double.
	lsl	x6, x3, #3

vector_loop:
	// If the remaining count (x5) is less than one full vector (x3), go to tail.
	cmp	x5, x3
	blt	tail_scalar

	// --- Process one full vector iteration ---
	// Load a full vector of double elements from array a into Z0.
	ld1d	{z0.d}, p0/z, [x0]
	// Use the SVE immediate multiply (mul) as a no–op (multiply by 1).
	mul	z0.d, z0.d, #1

	// Load a full vector of double elements from array b into Z1.
	ld1d	{z1.d}, p0/z, [x1]
	// Compute element–wise: result = a + b.
	fadd	z1.d, z0.d, z1.d
	// Store the result (in Z1) back into array b.
	st1d	{z1.d}, p0, [x1]

	// Update the pointers by adding the byte stride.
	add	x0, x0, x6
	add	x1, x1, x6
	// Decrement the remaining element count by the vector’s width (number of doubles).
	sub	x5, x5, x3
	b		vector_loop

tail_scalar:
	// --- Tail loop: process any remaining elements one by one ---
	cbz	x5, fun_return
tail_loop_scalar_start:
	ldr	d0, [x0]         // load one double from array a
	ldr	d1, [x1]         // load one double from array b
	fadd	d0, d0, d1       // compute: d0 = d0 + d1
	str	d0, [x1]         // store the result back to array b
	add	x0, x0, #8       // advance pointer a by 8 bytes
	add	x1, x1, #8       // advance pointer b by 8 bytes
	subs	x5, x5, #1
	bne		tail_loop_scalar_start

fun_return:
	mov	w0, wzr
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	fun, .-fun

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Function: main
	//   Standard C startup calling puts and printf.
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.globl	main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main, @function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	// Prologue: Save FP & LR.
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!         
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 32
	str	x19, [sp, #16]
	mov	x29, sp
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 32
	.cfi_offset w19, -16
	.cfi_offset w30, -24
	.cfi_offset w29, -32

	adrp	x0, .Lstr
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:.Lstr
	bl	puts

	adrp	x19, .L.str.1
	add	x19, x19, :lo12:.L.str.1
	fmov	d0, #6.00000000
	mov	x0, x19
	mov	w1, wzr
	bl	printf

	fmov	d0, #6.00000000
	mov	x0, x19
	mov	w1, #1
	bl	printf

	fmov	d0, #6.00000000
	mov	x0, x19
	mov	w1, #2
	bl	printf

	fmov	d0, #6.00000000
	mov	x0, x19
	mov	w1, #3
	bl	printf

	fmov	d0, #6.00000000
	mov	x0, x19
	mov	w1, #4
	bl	printf

	mov	w0, wzr
	.cfi_def_cfa wsp, 32
	ldr	x19, [sp, #16]
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #32
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
	.cfi_restore w19
	.cfi_restore w30
	.cfi_restore w29
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
	.size	main, .-main

	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Read–only data sections
	//---------------------------------------------------------------------
	.type	.L.str.1, @object
	.section	.rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1
.L.str.1:
	.asciz	"b[%d] = %f\n"
	.size	.L.str.1, 12

	.type	.Lstr, @object
	.section	.rodata,"a",@progbits
.Lstr:
	.asciz	"Result in array b after fun(a, b, size):"
	.size	.Lstr, 41

	.ident	"Translated to AArch64+SVE"
	.section	".note.GNU-stack","",@progbits
	.end

main:
        // Set up predicate for one active element (lane 0)
        mov     x16, #1
        whilelo p0.d, xzr, x16           // p0 active only for indices [0,1)
        // Use an eor (immediate) example --
        dup     z20.d, xzr                // initialize z20 = 0 in all lanes (using the 64‐bit zero)
        mov     x17, #1
        dup     z16.d, x17                // duplicate immediate “1” into z16
        eor     z20.d, p0, z20.d, z16.d   // z20 = 0 xor 1 = 1

        // Load our “constants” into vector registers (all operations act only on lane 0)
        mov     x17, #-6148914691236517206
        dup     z11.d, x17                // z11 <- 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
        mov     x17, #-6148914691236517206
        dup     z12.d, x17                // z12 <- same constant (to be fixed later)
        mov     x17, #144
        dup     z8.d, x17                 // z8 <- 144 (original w8)
        mov     x17, #287
        dup     z9.d, x17                 // z9 <- 287 (original w9)
        mov     x17, #1
        dup     z10.d, x17                // z10 <- 1   (original w10)

        // Emulate: movk x11, #43691
        //   x11 = (x11 & ~0xffff) | 43691
        mov     x17, 0xffffffffffff0000   // mask to clear low 16 bits
        dup     z16.d, x17
        and     z11.d, p0, z11.d, z16.d
        mov     x17, #43691
        dup     z16.d, x17
        orr     z11.d,  p0, z11.d, z16.d

        // Emulate: movk x12, #10922, lsl #48  
        //   x12 = (x12 & ~(0xffff << 48)) | (10922 << 48)
        mov     x17, 0x0000ffffffffffff   // mask: clear bits[63:48]
        dup     z16.d, x17
        and     z12.d, p0, z12.d, z16.d
        mov     x17, #10922
        dup     z16.d, x17
        lsl     z16.d, p0, z16.d, #48
        orr     z12.d, p0, z12.d, z16.d

        b       LBB0_2

// Loop update label
LBB0_1:
        mov     x17, #1
        dup     z16.d, x17
        add     z8.d, p0, z8.d, z16.d      // z8 := z8 + 1
        mov     x17, #2
        dup     z16.d, x17
        add     z9.d, p0, z9.d, z16.d      // z9 := z9 + 2

// Main inner‐loop (LBB0_2)
LBB0_2:
        mul     z1.d, p0, z9.d, z8.d       // z1 := z9 * z8
        lsl     z16.d, p0, z1.d, #1        // compute (z1 << 1)
        add     z13.d, p0, z1.d, z16.d      // z13 := z1 + (z1<<1)   [= 3*z1]
        lsl     z16.d, p0, z13.d, #3        // shift: (z13 << 3)
        orr     z13.d, p0, z10.d, z16.d     // z13 := z10 OR (z13<<3)

        ucvtf   z0.d, p0, z13.d            // convert unsigned int -> double FP
        fsqrt   z0.d, p0, z0.d             // take FP square-root
        fcvtzu  z14.d, p0, z0.d            // convert FP -> unsigned int

        mla     z15.d, p0, z14.d, z11.d, z11.d   // madd: z15 := (z14 * z11) + z11
        mul     z14.d, p0, z14.d, z14.d    // z14 := z14 * z14

        umov    x19, z14.d[0]             // extract lane0 of z14 -> x19
        umov    x18, z13.d[0]             // extract lane0 of z13 -> x18
        cmp     x19, x18
        b.hi    LBB0_1

        // Second check block:
        lsl     z16.d, p0, z1.d, #3        // z16 := z1 << 3
        orr     z14.d, p0, z10.d, z16.d     // z14 := z10 OR (z1<<3)
        ucvtf   z0.d, p0, z14.d
        fsqrt   z0.d, p0, z0.d
        fcvtzu  z0.d, p0, z0.d
        mov     z13.d, z0.d               // z13 := converted result
        mul     z15.d, p0, z13.d, z13.d    // z15 := z13 * z13

        umov    x19, z15.d[0]
        umov    x18, z14.d[0]
        cmp     x19, x18
        b.ne    LBB0_1

        umov    x19, z13.d[0]             // test LSB of z13
        tbz     x19, #0, LBB0_1           // if bit0 is zero, branch to LBB0_1

        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
        ret

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.file	"problem45.s"
	.globl	main
	.p2align	2

main:
	// Set up predicate for one active element (lane 0)
	    mov	    x16, #1
	    whilelo p0, xzr, x16              // p0 active only for indices [0,1)
	// Use an eor example --
	    dup	    z20.d, xzr                 // initialize z20 = 0 in all lanes (using 64‐bit zero)
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z16.d, x17                 // duplicate immediate “1” into z16
	    eor	    z20.d, p0, z20.d, z16.d     // z20 = 0 xor 1 = 1

	// Load our “constants” into vector registers (only lane 0 is used)
	    mov	    x17, #-6148914691236517206
	    dup	    z11.d, x17                 // z11 <- 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
	    mov	    x17, #-6148914691236517206
	    dup	    z12.d, x17                 // z12 <- same constant (to be fixed later)
	    mov	    x17, #144
	    dup	    z8.d, x17                  // z8 <- 144 (original w8)
	    mov	    x17, #287
	    dup	    z9.d, x17                  // z9 <- 287 (original w9)
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z10.d, x17                 // z10 <- 1   (original w10)

	// Emulate: movk x11, #43691
	//   x11 = (x11 & ~0xffff) | 43691
	    mov	    x17, 0xffffffffffff0000     // mask to clear low 16 bits
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    and	    z11.d, p0, z11.d, z16.d
	    mov	    x17, #43691
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    orr	    z11.d, p0, z11.d, z16.d

	// Emulate: movk x12, #10922, lsl #48  
	//   x12 = (x12 & ~(0xffff << 48)) | (10922 << 48)
	    mov	    x17, 0x0000ffffffffffff     // mask: clear bits[63:48]
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    and	    z12.d, p0, z12.d, z16.d
	    mov	    x17, #10922
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0, z16.d, #48
	    orr	    z12.d, p0, z12.d, z16.d

// Loop update label
LBB0_1:
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    add	    z8.d, p0, z8.d, z16.d       // z8 := z8 + 1
	    mov	    x17, #2
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    add	    z9.d, p0, z9.d, z16.d       // z9 := z9 + 2

// Main inner‐loop (LBB0_2)
LBB0_2:
	    mul	    z1.d, p0, z9.d, z8.d        // z1 := z9 * z8
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0, z1.d, #1         // (z1 << 1)
	    add	    z13.d, p0, z1.d, z16.d       // z13 := z1 + (z1<<1) = 3*z1
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0, z13.d, #3         // (z13 << 3)
	    orr	    z13.d, p0, z10.d, z16.d      // z13 := z10 OR (z13<<3)

	    ucvtf	z0.d, p0, z13.d              // convert unsigned int -> double FP
	    fsqrt	z0.d, p0, z0.d               // take FP square-root
	    fcvtzu	z14.d, p0, z0.d              // convert FP -> unsigned int

	    mul	    z14.d, p0, z14.d, z14.d      // z14 := z14 * z14

	    umov    x18, z13.d[0]               // extract lane0 of z13 -> x18

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.file	"problem45.s"
	.globl	main
	.p2align	2

main:
	// Set up predicate for one active element (lane 0)
	    mov	    x16, #1
	    whilelo p0.d, xzr, x16              // p0 active only for indices [0,1)
	// Instead of dup’ing from xzr (which is not accepted) use a reg holding 0:
	    mov	    x15, #0
	    dup	    z20.d, x15                  // z20 = 0 in all lanes
	    
	    // Use an eor example --
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z16.d, x17                  // duplicate immediate “1” into z16
	    eor	    z20.d, p0/m, z20.d, z16.d     // z20 = 0 xor 1 = 1

	// Load our “constants” into vector registers (only lane 0 is used)
	    mov	    x17, #-6148914691236517206
	    dup	    z11.d, x17                 // z11 <- 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
	    mov	    x17, #-6148914691236517206
	    dup	    z12.d, x17                 // z12 <- same constant (to be fixed later)
	    mov	    x17, #144
	    dup	    z8.d, x17                  // z8 <- 144 (original w8)
	    mov	    x17, #287
	    dup	    z9.d, x17                  // z9 <- 287 (original w9)
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z10.d, x17                 // z10 <- 1   (original w10)

	// Emulate: movk x11, #43691 
	//   x11 = (x11 & ~0xffff) | 43691
	    mov	    x17, 0xffffffffffff0000     // mask to clear low 16 bits
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    and	    z11.d, p0/m, z11.d, z16.d
	    mov	    x17, #43691
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    orr	    z11.d, p0/m, z11.d, z16.d

	// Emulate: movk x12, #10922, lsl #48  
	//   x12 = (x12 & ~(0xffff << 48)) | (10922 << 48)
	    mov	    x17, 0x0000ffffffffffff     // mask: clear bits[63:48]
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    and	    z12.d, p0/m, z12.d, z16.d
	    mov	    x17, #10922
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0/m, z16.d, #48	// destination must equal source
	    orr	    z12.d, p0/m, z12.d, z16.d

	    b	    LBB0_2

// Loop update label
LBB0_1:
	    mov	    x17, #1
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    add	    z8.d, p0/m, z8.d, z16.d       // z8 := z8 + 1
	    mov	    x17, #2
	    dup	    z16.d, x17
	    add	    z9.d, p0/m, z9.d, z16.d       // z9 := z9 + 2

// Main inner‐loop (LBB0_2)
LBB0_2:
	    // Compute z1 = z9 * z8. (For SVE “mul” the destination must equal the first source.)
	    movprfx z1, z9
	    mul	    z1.d, p0/m, z1.d, z8.d

	    // Compute z16 = z1 << 1.
	    movprfx z16, z1
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0/m, z16.d, #1

	    // Compute z13 = z1 + (z1 << 1) = 3*z1.
	    movprfx z13, z1
	    add	    z13.d, p0/m, z13.d, z16.d

	    // Compute z16 = z13 << 3.
	    movprfx z16, z13
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0/m, z16.d, #3

	    // Compute z13 = z10 OR (z13 << 3). (dest must equal first source)
	    movprfx z13, z10
	    orr	    z13.d, p0/m, z13.d, z16.d

	    ucvtf	z0.d, p0/m, z13.d              // convert unsigned int -> double FP
	    fsqrt	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d               // take FP square-root
	    fcvtzu	z14.d, p0/m, z0.d              // convert FP -> unsigned int

	    // Compute z15 = (z14 * z11) + z11.
	    // For MLA the accumulate operand (last) must equal the destination.
	    // (Using the fact that z15 has been set equal to z11 via movprfx.)
	    movprfx z15, z11
	    mla	    z15.d, p0/m, z15.d, z14.d, z15.d

	    // Square z14 in place.
	    mul	    z14.d, p0/m, z14.d, z14.d

	    umov    x19, z14, #0               // extract lane0 of z14 -> x19
	    umov    x18, z13, #0               // extract lane0 of z13 -> x18
	    cmp	    x19, x18
	    b.hi    LBB0_1

	    // Second check block:
	    // Compute z16 = z1 << 3.
	    movprfx z16, z1
	    lsl	    z16.d, p0/m, z16.d, #3

	    // Compute z14 = z10 OR (z1 << 3).
	    movprfx z14, z10
	    orr	    z14.d, p0/m, z14.d, z16.d

	    ucvtf	z0.d, p0/m, z14.d
	    fsqrt	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d
	    fcvtzu	z0.d, p0/m, z0.d
	    mov	    z13.d, z0.d                // (regular move is OK here)

	    // Compute z15 = z13 * z13.
	    movprfx z15, z13
	    mul	    z15.d, p0/m, z15.d, z13.d

	    umov    x19, z15, #0
	    umov    x18, z14, #0
	    cmp	    x19, x18
	    b.ne    LBB0_1

	    umov    x19, z13, #0              // test LSB of z13
	    tbz	    x19, #0, LBB0_1            // if bit0 is zero, branch
	    
	    // Print result (use the standard scalar ABI)
	    stp	    x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	    mov	    x29, sp
	    adrp    x0, L_str
	    add	    x0, x0, :lo12:L_str
	    bl	    printf
	    mov	    w0, wzr
	    ldp	    x29, x30, [sp], #16
	    ret
Lfunc_end0:
	    .size	main, . - main

	    movprfx z8, z0
	    add	    z8.d, p0/m, z8.d, z16.d

main:                                   // @main
	.cfi_startproc
	/* Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements */
	ptrue p0.d

	/* Initialize some constants */
	mov	x11, #-6148914691236517206      // 0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
	mov	x12, #-6148914691236517206
	mov	w8, #144                        // 0x90
	mov	w9, #287                        // 0x11f
	mov	w10, #1                         // constant 1
	movk	x11, #43691
	movk	x12, #10922, lsl #48
	b	.LBB0_2

.LBB0_1:                                // in Loop: Header of update block
	/* Update loop indices */
	add	x8, x8, #1
	add	x9, x9, #2

.LBB0_2:                                // First part of inner loop
	mul	x1, x9, x8
	add	x13, x1, x1, lsl #1            // x13 = 3*x1

	/* 
	   Replace: orr x13, x10, x13, lsl #3 
	   with a vector sequence:
	     – duplicate the scalar into z13,
	     – shift left by 3 (using predicate p0/m), 
	     – then use “EOR immediate 1” (note: for SVE the destination must match the source)
	     – finally extract a lane using UMOV.
	*/
	dup	z13.d, x13               // duplicate scalar x13 into every 64‐bit lane of z13
	lsl	z13.d, p0/m, z13.d, #3     // compute (x13 << 3)
	eor	z13.d, z13.d, #1           // XOR immediate 1 (same as ORR 1 since the low 3 bits are zero)
	umov	x13, z13.d, #0           // extract lowest element back to x13

	ucvtf	d0, x13
	fsqrt	d0, d0
	fcvtzu	x14, d0
	madd	x15, x14, x11, x11
	mul	x14, x14, x14
	cmp	x14, x13
	ror	x15, x15, #1
	ccmp	x15, x12, #2, eq
	b.hi	.LBB0_1

.LBB0_3:                                // Second inner portion
	/* 
	   Replace: orr x14, x10, x1, lsl #3 
	   with a similar SVE sequence.
	*/
	dup	z1.d, x1                // duplicate scalar x1 into every lane of z1
	lsl	z1.d, p0/m, z1.d, #3       // compute (x1 << 3)
	eor	z1.d, z1.d, #1             // XOR immediate 1 (destination must equal source)
	umov	x14, z1.d, #0            // move result into x14

	ucvtf	d0, x14
	fsqrt	d0, d0
	fcvtzu	x13, d0
	mul	x15, x13, x13
	cmp	x15, x14
	b.ne	.LBB0_1

.LBB0_4:
	tbz	w13, #0, .LBB0_1

.LBB0_5:
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!       // 16-byte folded spill

	mov	x29, sp

.globl  main                            // -- Begin function main
        .type   main,@function
main:                                       // @main
        .cfi_startproc
        /* Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements */
        ptrue p0.d

        /* Initialize some constants */
        mov     x11, #-6148914691236517206      // 0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
        mov     x12, #-6148914691236517206
        mov     w8, #144                        // 0x90
        mov     w9, #287                        // 0x11f
        mov     w10, #1                         // constant 1
        movk    x11, #43691
        movk    x12, #10922, lsl #48
        b       .LBB0_2

.LBB0_1:                                   // in Loop: Header of update block
        /* Update loop indices */
        add     x8, x8, #1
        add     x9, x9, #2

.LBB0_2:                                   // First part of inner loop
        mul     x1, x9, x8
        add     x13, x1, x1, lsl #1            // x13 = 3*x1

        /* 
           Replace: orr x13, x10, x13, lsl #3 
           with a vector sequence:
             – duplicate the scalar into z13,
             – shift left by 3 (using predicate p0/m), 
             – then use “EOR immediate 1” (note: for SVE the destination must match the source)
             – finally extract a lane using UMOV.
        */
        dup     z13.d, x13                 // duplicate scalar x13 into every 64‐bit lane of z13
        lsl     z13.d, p0/m, z13.d, #3       // compute (x13 << 3)
        eor     z13.d, z13.d, #1             // XOR immediate 1 (same as ORR 1 since the low 3 bits are zero)
        umov    x13, z13.d[#0]              // extract the lowest element (fixed syntax)

        ucvtf   d0, x13
        fsqrt   d0, d0
        fcvtzu  x14, d0
        madd    x15, x14, x11, x11
        mul     x14, x14, x14
        cmp     x14, x13
        ror     x15, x15, #1
        ccmp    x15, x12, #2, eq
        b.hi    .LBB0_1

.LBB0_3:                                   // Second inner portion
        /* 
           Replace: orr x14, x10, x1, lsl #3 
           with a similar SVE sequence.
        */
        dup     z1.d, x1                  // duplicate scalar x1 into every lane of z1
        lsl     z1.d, p0/m, z1.d, #3        // compute (x1 << 3)
        eor     z1.d, z1.d, #1              // XOR immediate 1 (destination must equal source)
        umov    x14, z1.d[#0]              // move result into x14 (fixed syntax)

        ucvtf   d0, x14
        fsqrt   d0, d0
        fcvtzu  x13, d0
        mul     x15, x13, x13
        cmp     x15, x14
        b.ne    .LBB0_1

.LBB0_4:
        tbz     w13, #0, .LBB0_1

        mov     x29, sp

        .cfi_offset w30, -8
        .cfi_offset w29, -16
        adrp    x0, .L.str
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str
        bl      printf
        mov     w0, wzr
        .cfi_def_cfa wsp, 16
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16         // 16-byte folded reload
        .cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
        .cfi_restore w30
        .cfi_restore w29

(predicate) 
Initial is e predicate from named constraint 
Set elements of the destination predicate to true if the element number satisfies the named predicate constraint or to false 
otherwise If the constraint specifies more elements than are available at the current vector length then all elements of the 
destination predicate are set to false 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception Does not set the condition flags

        .global two_pow
        .p2align 2
two_pow:
        // If the count in x0 is zero, return 1.
        cmp     x0, #0
        beq     two_pow_zero

        // Load the divisor “base” from memory.
        adrp    x8, base
        ldr     x9, [x8, :lo12:base]       // x9 = base (10^10)

        // Set accumulator = 1 (in a scalar register, then duplicate into vector register Z0).
        mov     x11, #1
        dup     z0.d, x11                 // z0.d <-- 1

        // Duplicate the divisor into vector register Z1.
        dup     z1.d, x9                  // z1.d <-- base

        // Load the pre‐computed magic multiplier M = 14757395259.
        ldr     x10, =14757395259
        dup     z2.d, x10                 // z2.d <-- magic constant

        // Initialize predicate: all lanes active.
        ptrue   p0.d

two_pow_loop:
        subs    x0, x0, #1                // decrement loop counter

        // Double the accumulator: 2*x.
        add     z0.d, p0/m, z0.d, z0.d

        // Compute: quotient = asr(smulh(accumulator, magic), 3)
        // To avoid destroying z0, make a copy of z0 into z3.
        orr     z3.d, p0/m, z0.d, z0.d
        smulh   z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d   // z3 = high half of (z0 * magic)
        asr     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, #3      // z3 = quotient = z3 >> 3

        // Compute product = quotient * divisor.
        mul     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z1.d   // z3 = quotient * base

        // New accumulator = (doubled accumulator) – (quotient * base).
        sub     z0.d, p0/m, z0.d, z3.d

        b.ne    two_pow_loop             // loop until x0 == 0

        // Return the result from lane 0.
        umov    x0, z0.d[0]
        ret

two_pow_zero:
        mov     x0, #1
        ret

        .global main
        .p2align 2
main:
        // Compute constant “base” (= 10^10) and store it.
        mov     x8, #58368
        mov     x9, #-31673
        movk    x8, #21515, lsl #16
        adrp    x11, base
        movk    x8, #2, lsl #32
        movk    x9, #65416, lsl #16
        str     x8, [x11, :lo12:base]

        // Initialize accumulator for inner loop.
        mov     x10, #1
        dup     z5.d, x10                // z5.d <-- 1

        // Load divisor “base” into vector register Z1.
        adrp    x8, base
        ldr     x8, [x8, :lo12:base]      // x8 = base
        dup     z1.d, x8                 // z1.d <-- base

        // Set up magic constant M = 14757395259 in Z2.
        ldr     x11, =14757395259
        dup     z2.d, x11                // z2.d <-- magic constant

        // Set predicate bits so that all lanes are active.
        ptrue   p0.d

main_loop:
        // Double the accumulator in z5.
        add     z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z5.d

        // Increment loop counter in x9 (using ADDS to update flags).
        adds    x9, x9, #1

        // Compute: quotient = asr(smulh(z5, magic), 3)
        // Copy z5 into z3 (using ORR to avoid destroying z5).
        orr     z3.d, p0/m, z5.d, z5.d
        smulh   z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d
        asr     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, #3

        // Compute product = quotient * base.
        mul     z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z1.d

        // New accumulator = (doubled value) – (quotient * base).
        sub     z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z3.d

        orr     x9, x9, #1

samples.tested_code:
// Tell the assembler we want SVE2 (which implies SVE) on Armv9a.
    .arch armv9a+sve2
    .text

    .global two_pow
    .p2align 2
// two_pow: computes 2^n mod base.
// Input:  x0 = n (number of iterations)
// Global variable "base" is a 64‐bit unsigned number.
two_pow:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // if (n==0) return 1:
    cbz      x0, two_pow_zero

    // Load “base” from memory into x9.
    adrp     x8, base
    ldr      x9, [x8, :lo12:base]

    // Set up predicate for 64‐bit (.d) elements.
    ptrue    p0.d

    // Initialize our vector “accumulator” to 1:
    mov      x10, #1
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 in every lane
    // Broadcast base into z1.
    dup      z1.d, x9          // z1 ← base

    // Compute magic = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base).
    mov      x11, -1           // x11 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    sdiv     x11, x11, x9      // magic constant in x11
    dup      z2.d, x11         // z2 ← magic

two_pow_loop:
    subs     x0, x0, #1        // decrement loop counter

    // Double the result:
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Compute high‐half multiplication:
    mov      z3, z0            // copy dividend into z3
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Adjust quotient: (q >> 1 << 1) + (q & 1)
    mov      z5, z3            // copy quotient candidate into z5
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1  // z5 = z3 >> 1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1  // z5 = z5 << 1  (clears lowest bit)
    dup      z7.d, #1         // create constant 1 in every lane
    mov      z6, z3            // copy quotient candidate into z6 for use in AND
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d  // z6 = z3 & 1
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d   // z5 = (q with lowest bit cleared) + (q & 1)
    mov      z3, z5            // store adjusted quotient back in z3

    // Multiply: quotient * base.
    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d

    // Subtract to get the remainder.
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    cbnz     x0, two_pow_loop

    // Extract the result from lane 0 using the NEON alias V0.
    umov     x0, v0.d[0]

    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

two_pow_zero:
    mov      x0, #1
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret


    .global main
    .p2align 2
// main: the inner loop here also uses magic division.
main:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // Set up some constants and write “base”
    mov      x8, #58368
    mov      x9, #-31673
    movk     x8, #21515, lsl #16
    adrp     x11, base
    // For a 64–bit constant, also update the upper half.
    movk     x8, #2, lsl #32
    movk     x9, #65416, lsl #16
    mov      x10, #1           // use x10 (64–bit) for dup

    str      x8, [x11, :lo12:base]

    // Set up the vector accumulator and magic constant.
    ptrue    p0.d
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 (accumulator)
    dup      z1.d, x8          // z1 ← base
    mov      x12, -1
    sdiv     x12, x12, x8      // magic constant = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base)
    dup      z2.d, x12         // z2 ← magic

inner_loop:
    // Double the accumulator.
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Also update the loop counter by 1 (setting the condition flags).
    adds     x9, x9, #1

    // Do the magic division on z0:
    mov      z3, z0            // copy into z3 so that destination equals first source
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d
    mov      z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    dup      z7.d, #1
    mov      z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d
    mov      z3, z5            // save adjusted quotient in z3

    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    // Loop while the updated x9 is lower than zero (unsigned comparison).
    blo      inner_loop

    // Set up frame for printf.
    mov      x29, sp
    mov      w9, #28433
    adr      x0, L_str
    add      x0, x0, :lo12:L_str

    // Extract the accumulator value from lane 0.
    umov     x10, v0.d[0]
    mul      x9, x10, x9
    orr      x9, x9, #0x1

    // Final “magic” division:
    mov      x12, -1
    sdiv     x12, x12, x8
    dup      z2.d, x12
    dup      z0.d, x9          // broadcast x9 into every lane
    mov      z3, z0
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d
    mov      z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    dup      z7.d, #1
    mov      z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d
    mov      z3, z5
    mul      z3.d, z3.d, z1.d
    umov     x10, v3.d[0]       // extract the computed quotient

    // Use msub (x1 = x9 − (x10×x8))
    msub     x1, x10, x8, x9

    bl       printf

    mov      w0, wzr
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

    .data
    .p2align 3

// Tell the assembler we want SVE2 (which implies SVE) on Armv9a.
    .arch armv9a+sve2
    .text

    .global two_pow
    .p2align 2
// two_pow: computes 2^n mod base.
// Input:  x0 = n (number of iterations)
// Global variable "base" is a 64‐bit unsigned number.
two_pow:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // if (n==0) return 1:
    cbz      x0, two_pow_zero

    // Load “base” from memory into x9.
    adrp     x8, base
    ldr      x9, [x8, :lo12:base]

    // Set up predicate for 64‐bit (.d) elements.
    ptrue    p0.d

    // Initialize our vector “accumulator” to 1:
    mov      x10, #1
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 in every lane
    // Broadcast base into z1.
    dup      z1.d, x9          // z1 ← base

    // Compute magic = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base).
    mov      x11, -1           // x11 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    sdiv     x11, x11, x9      // magic constant in x11
    dup      z2.d, x11         // z2 ← magic

two_pow_loop:
    subs     x0, x0, #1        // decrement loop counter

    // Double the result:
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Compute high‐half multiplication:
    orr      z3.d, p0/m, z0.d, z0.d   // copy dividend into z3
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Adjust quotient: (q >> 1 << 1) + (q & 1)
    orr      z5.d, p0/m, z3.d, z3.d   // copy quotient candidate into z5
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z3 >> 1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z5 << 1  (clears lowest bit)
    dup      z7.d, #1                 // create constant 1 in every lane
    orr      z6.d, p0/m, z3.d, z3.d   // copy quotient candidate into z6 for use in AND
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d    // z6 = z3 & 1
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d    // z5 = (q with lowest bit cleared) + (q & 1)
    orr      z3.d, p0/m, z5.d, z5.d    // store adjusted quotient back in z3

    // Multiply: quotient * base.
    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d

    // Subtract to get the remainder.
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    cbnz     x0, two_pow_loop

    // Extract the result from lane 0 using the NEON alias V0.
    umov     x0, v0.d[0]

    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

two_pow_zero:
    mov      x0, #1
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret


    .global main
    .p2align 2
// main: the inner loop here also uses magic division.
main:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // Set up some constants and write “base”
    mov      x8, #58368
    mov      x9, #-31673
    movk     x8, #21515, lsl #16
    adrp     x11, base

    ptrue    p0.d
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 (accumulator)

    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

// Tell the assembler we want SVE2 (which implies SVE) on Armv9a.
    .arch armv9a+sve2
    .text

    .global two_pow
    .p2align 2
// two_pow: computes 2^n mod base.
// Input:  x0 = n (number of iterations)
// Global variable "base" is a 64‐bit unsigned number.
two_pow:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // if (n==0) return 1:
    cbz      x0, two_pow_zero

    // Load “base” from memory into x9.
    adrp     x8, base
    ldr      x9, [x8, :lo12:base]

    // Set up predicate for 64‐bit (.d) elements.
    ptrue    p0.d

    // Initialize our vector “accumulator” to 1:
    mov      x10, #1
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 in every lane
    // Broadcast base into z1.
    dup      z1.d, x9          // z1 ← base

    // Compute magic = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base).
    mov      x11, -1           // x11 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    sdiv     x11, x11, x9      // magic constant in x11
    dup      z2.d, x11         // z2 ← magic

two_pow_loop:
    subs     x0, x0, #1        // decrement loop counter

    // Double the result:
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Copy dividend into z3.
    mov      z3, z0
    // Compute high‐half multiplication:
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Copy quotient candidate into z5.
    mov      z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z3 >> 1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z5 << 1  (clears lowest bit)
    dup      z7.d, #1                 // create constant 1 in every lane

    // Copy quotient candidate into z6 for use in AND.
    mov      z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d    // z6 = z3 & 1
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d    // z5 = (q with lowest bit cleared) + (q & 1)

    // Store adjusted quotient back in z3.
    mov      z3, z5

    // Multiply: quotient * base.
    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d

    // Subtract to get the remainder.
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    cbnz     x0, two_pow_loop

    // Extract the result from lane 0 using the NEON alias V0.
    umov     x0, v0.d[0]

    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

two_pow_zero:
    mov      x0, #1
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret


    .global main
    .p2align 2
// main: the inner loop here also uses magic division.
main:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // Set up some constants and write “base”
    mov      x8, #58368
    mov      x9, #-31673
    movk     x8, #21515, lsl #16
    adrp     x11, base
    // For a 64–bit constant, also update the upper half.
    movk     x8, #2, lsl #32
    movk     x9, #65416, lsl #16
    mov      x10, #1           // use x10 (64–bit) for dup

    str      x8, [x11, :lo12:base]

    // Set up the vector accumulator and magic constant.
    ptrue    p0.d
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 (accumulator)
    dup      z1.d, x8          // z1 ← base
    mov      x12, -1
    sdiv     x12, x12, x8      // magic constant = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base)
    dup      z2.d, x12         // z2 ← magic

inner_loop:
    // Double the accumulator.
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Also update the loop counter by 1 (setting the condition flags).
    adds     x9, x9, #1

    // Copy z0 into z3 so that destination equals first source.
    mov      z3, z0
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Copy quotient candidate into z5.
    mov      z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    dup      z7.d, #1

    mov      z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d
    // Save adjusted quotient in z3.
    mov      z3, z5

    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    mov      w9, #28433

    add      x0, x0, :lo12:L_str

// Tell the assembler we want SVE2 (which implies SVE) on Armv9a.
    .arch armv9a+sve2
    .text

    .global two_pow
    .p2align 2
// two_pow: computes 2^n mod base.
// Input:  x0 = n (number of iterations)
// Global variable "base" is a 64‐bit unsigned number.
two_pow:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // if (n==0) return 1:
    cbz      x0, two_pow_zero

    // Load “base” from memory into x9.
    adrp     x8, base
    ldr      x9, [x8, :lo12:base]

    // Set up predicate for 64‐bit (.d) elements.
    ptrue    p0.d

    // Initialize our vector “accumulator” to 1:
    mov      x10, #1
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 in every lane
    // Broadcast base into z1.
    dup      z1.d, x9          // z1 ← base

    // Compute magic = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base).
    mov      x11, -1           // x11 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    sdiv     x11, x11, x9      // magic constant in x11
    dup      z2.d, x11         // z2 ← magic

two_pow_loop:
    subs     x0, x0, #1        // decrement loop counter

    // Double the result:
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Copy dividend into z3.
    movprfx z3, z0
    // Compute high‐half multiplication:
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Copy quotient candidate into z5.
    movprfx z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z3 >> 1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1      // z5 = z5 << 1  (clears lowest bit)
    dup      z7.d, #1                 // create constant 1 in every lane

    // Copy quotient candidate into z6 for use in AND.
    movprfx z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d    // z6 = z3 & 1
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d    // z5 = (q with lowest bit cleared) + (q & 1)

    // Store adjusted quotient back in z3.
    movprfx z3, z5

    // Multiply: quotient * base.
    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d

    // Subtract to get the remainder.
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    cbnz     x0, two_pow_loop

    // Extract the result from lane 0 using the NEON alias V0.
    umov     x0, v0.d[0]

    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

two_pow_zero:
    mov      x0, #1
    ldp      x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret


    .global main
    .p2align 2
// main: the inner loop here also uses magic division.
main:
    stp      x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov      x29, sp

    // Set up some constants and write “base”
    mov      x8, #58368
    mov      x9, #-31673
    movk     x8, #21515, lsl #16
    adrp     x11, base
    // For a 64–bit constant, also update the upper half.
    movk     x8, #2, lsl #32
    movk     x9, #65416, lsl #16
    mov      x10, #1           // use x10 (64–bit) for dup

    str      x8, [x11, :lo12:base]

    // Set up the vector accumulator and magic constant.
    ptrue    p0.d
    dup      z0.d, x10         // z0 ← 1 (accumulator)
    dup      z1.d, x8          // z1 ← base
    mov      x12, -1
    sdiv     x12, x12, x8      // magic constant = floor(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF/base)
    dup      z2.d, x12         // z2 ← magic

inner_loop:
    // Double the accumulator.
    add      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d

    // Also update the loop counter by 1 (setting the condition flags).
    adds     x9, x9, #1

    // Copy z0 into z3 so that destination equals first source.
    movprfx z3, z0
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

    // Copy quotient candidate into z5.
    movprfx z5, z3
    asr      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    lsl      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, #1
    dup      z7.d, #1
    // Copy quotient candidate into z6 for use in AND.
    movprfx z6, z3
    and      z6.d, p0/m, z6.d, z7.d
    add      z5.d, p0/m, z5.d, z6.d
    // Save adjusted quotient in z3.
    movprfx z3, z5

    mul      z4.d, z3.d, z1.d
    sub      z0.d, z0.d, z4.d

    // Loop while the updated x9 is lower than zero (unsigned comparison).
    blo      inner_loop

    // Set up frame for printf.
    mov      x29, sp
    mov      w9, #28433
    adr      x0, L_str
    add      x0, x0, :lo12:L_str

    // Extract the accumulator value from lane 0.
    umov     x10, v0.d[0]
    mul      x9, x10, x9
    orr      x9, x9, #0x1

    // Final “magic” division:
    mov      x12, -1
    sdiv     x12, x12, x8
    dup      z2.d, x12
    dup      z0.d, x9          // broadcast x9 into every lane
    // Copy into z3 so that destination equals first source.
    movprfx z3, z0
    smulh    z3.d, p0/m, z3.d, z2.d

samples.generated: Below is one acceptable answer. In our fixed version we make these changes: 1. For the INDEX instruction the operands are swapped so that the immediate (which must be in [–16,15]) comes last. 2. All “mov” instructions that merely copy a whole Z register are written without a “.s” suffix. 3. Predicate registers are always written without a type suffix (for example, we write “p0” not “p0.s”). (Instructions that act element‐wise on Z registers still show “.s” or “.b”.) 4. Because SVE “str”/“ldr” for predicate registers do not allow write‐back addressing, we manually adjust SP (using “sub”/“add”) instead of writing “[sp, #-16]!” or using post–index addressing. One acceptable full solution is given below. (Any equivalent solution that uses the same concepts is correct.) .arch_extension sve2 .text .global main .type main, @function main: // Function prologue: make room for our frame and temporary storage. stp x29, x30, [sp, #-32]! mov x29, sp // rdvl: read (vector length in bytes)×#1 into x0. rdvl x0, #1 // ptrue: set all 32‐bit lanes active in predicate p0. ptrue p0 // Load the address of the grid into x1. adrp x1, .L__const_main_grid add x1, x1, :lo12:.L__const_main_grid // ld1w: load a vector of 32‐bit words from memory into z0. ld1w {z0.s}, p0/z, [x1] // Create an index vector in z1 starting at 0, incrementing by 1. // (Note: The syntax is adjusted so that the immediate comes last.) mov x2, #1 index z1.s, x2, #0 // Copy z0 into z2 then subtract 5 from every 32‐bit element. mov z2, z0 sub z2.s, z2.s, #5 // Copy z2 into z3 then shift each element right (logical shift) by 1. mov z3, z2 lsr z3.s, p0/m, z3.s, #1 // Copy z3 into z4 then shift left each element by 1. mov z4, z3 lsl z4.s, p0/m, z4.s, #1 // Copy z4 into z5 then AND each 32‐bit element with 0xFF. mov z5, z4 and z5.s, z5.s, #0xFF // Copy z5 into z6 then negate each active element. mov z6, z5 neg z6.s, p0/m, z6.s // Use splice: set z7 = z6 and splice in parts from z0. mov z7, z6 splice z7.s, p0, z7.s, z0.s // Unzip (i.e. extract even‐numbered lanes) from z7 and z6 into z8. uzp1 z8.s, z7.s, z6.s // Use movprfx to copy z8 into z9. movprfx z9, z8 // whilels: produce a predicate p1 marking the active lanes from xzr up to x0. whilels p1, xzr, x0 // cntw: count the number of active lanes in p1. cntw x3, p1 // rev: reverse the order of all elements in predicate p1 into p2. rev p2, p1 // Store the predicate register p2 on the stack. sub sp, sp, #16 str p2, [sp] // lastb: extract the last active byte from z0;         str     w1, [x0]

.global	is_prime
	.p2align	2
	.type	is_prime,@function
is_prime:
	// if(n < 4) return 1;
	cmp	w0, #4
	b.lt	is_prime_return_one

	// else set candidate divisor = 2
	mov	w8, #2
is_prime_loop:
	// remainder = n – (n/w8)*w8
	sdiv	w9, w0, w8
	msub	w9, w9, w8, w0
	cbz	w9, is_prime_return_zero
	// candidate++ 
	add	w8, w8, #1
	// if (candidate*candidate <= n) then loop
	mul	w10, w8, w8
	cmp	w10, w0
	ble	is_prime_loop

	// no divisor found: return 1
is_prime_return_one:
	mov	w0, #1
	// --- SVE demonstration: broadcast result then subtract immediate 0 ---
	dup	z0.s, w0
	sub	z0.s, z0.s, #0
	umov	w0, z0.s[#0]
	ret

is_prime_return_zero:
	mov	w0, wzr
	dup	z0.s, w0
	sub	z0.s, z0.s, #0
	umov	w0, z0.s[#0]
	ret
	.size	is_prime, .-is_prime


	.global	aux
	.p2align	2
	.type	aux,@function
aux:
	// Standard prologue:
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
	mov	x29, sp
	stp	x20, x19, [sp, #64]
	stp	x22, x21, [sp, #48]
	stp	x24, x23, [sp, #32]
	str	x25, [sp, #16]

	adrp	x8, nb_primes
	ldrsw	x23, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]
	cmp	w23, w0
	b.ne	aux_not_equal
	// if equal, return 1
	mov	w20, #1
	b	aux_epilogue

aux_not_equal:
	cmp	w23, w0
	mov	w19, w1
	mov	w20, wzr
	ccmp	w1, #0, #4, gt
	b.eq	aux_epilogue
	sxtw	x21, w0
	adrp	x24, primes
	add	x24, x24, :lo12:primes
aux_loop:
	ldr	w25, [x24, x21, lsl #2]
	add	x21, x21, #1
	mov	w22, w19
aux_inner_loop:
	sdiv	w22, w22, w25
	mov	w0, w21
	mov	w1, w22
	bl	aux
	add	w20, w0, w20
	cbnz	w22,	aux_inner_loop
	cmp	x21, x23
	b.ne	aux_loop

aux_epilogue:
	mov	w0, w20
	// --- SVE demonstration before return ---
	dup	z1.s, w0
	sub	z1.s, z1.s, #0
	umov	w0, z1.s[#0]
	ldp	x20, x19, [sp, #64]
	ldp	x22, x21, [sp, #48]
	ldp	x24, x23, [sp, #32])
	ldr	x25, [sp, #16]
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #80
	ret
	.size	aux, .-aux


	.global	main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main,@function
main:
	// Initialize nb_primes and primes data.
	adrp	x8, nb_primes
	mov	w9, #2			// candidate number starting at 2
	adrp	x11, primes
	add	x11, x11, :lo12:primes
	ldr	w10, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]
	// Outer loop header:
	b	.LBB2_3

.LBB2_1:
	// Store prime candidate in primes array
	add	w12, w10, #1
	str	w9, [x11, w10, sxtw #2]
	mov	w10, w12
	str	w12, [x8, :lo12:nb_primes]

.LBB2_2:
	// Outer loop: candidate++
	add	w9, w9, #1
	cmp	w9, #101
	b.eq	.LBB2_7

.LBB2_3:
	// For numbers less than 4, immediately prime.
	cmp	w9, #4
	b.lo	.LBB2_1

.LBB2_4:
	// Begin inner (divisibility) test:
	mov	w12, #2

.LBB2_5:
	udiv	w13, w9, w12
	msub	w13, w13, w12, w9	// remainder = w9 - (w9/w12)*w12
	cbz	w13,	.LBB2_2		// if divisible, not prime --> increment outer

.LBB2_6:
	add	w12, w12, #1
	mul	w13, w12, w12
	cmp	w13, w9
	b.ls	.LBB2_5		// while (w12*w12 <= w9), test divisibility
	b	.LBB2_1		// if no divisor found, then prime

.LBB2_7:
	// End-of-loop: call aux and then printf the result.
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov	x29, sp
	mov	w1, #51712
	mov	w0, wzr
	movk	w1, #15258, lsl #16
	// --- SVE demonstration: use sub immediate on w1 ---
	dup	z0.s, w1
	sub	z0.s, z0.s, #0
	umov	w1, z0.s[#0]
	bl	aux
	mov	w1, w0
	adrp	x0, L_str
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:L_str
	bl	printf
	mov	w0, wzr
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret
	.size	main, .-main

// Use an SVE2‐capable target
    .text
    .arch armv8.5-a+sve2
    .global powm
    .type powm, @function
powm:
    // Base-case: if exponent == 0 return 1.
    cbz    w1, powm_base

    // Function prologue.
    stp    x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!
    mov    x29, sp
    stp    x19, xzr, [sp, #-16]!   // save x19 (base operand)

    // Save original base in x19.
    mov    x19, x0

    // Test the low–order bit of exponent.
    tbnz   w1, #0, powm_odd

    // EVEN exponent branch:
    cmp    w1, #0
    mov    w0, w19            // pass base operand into recursive call
    cinc   w8, w1, lt        // w8 = (w1+1) if condition (used to compute half)
    asr    w1, w8, #1        // w1 = half exponent
    bl     powm              // recursive call; result in w0

    // Compute square:  w8 = w0 * w0.
    mul    w8, w0, w0

    // Set up constants:
    // Constant1 = 0x10524DD3   (constructed from 19923 and 4194)
    mov    w9, #19923
    movk   w9, #4194, lsl #16
    // Constant2 = 250
    mov    w10, #250

    // Compute: umull x9, w8, w9, then lsr x9, x9, #36.
    umull  x9, w8, w9
    lsr    x9, x9, #36

    // Now compute: result = w8 - (x9 * 250)
    // We “simulate” a multiply-subtract using SVE mls (indexed).
    ptrue    p0.d                // set predicate p0 for all 64–bit (d) lanes

    // To operate on scalars via SVE we temporarily move our values (in x8, x9, x10)
    // into vector registers using a stack‐based temporary buffer.
    // --- Load w8 into vector register Z0.
    sub      sp, sp, #16         // allocate 16 bytes
    str      x8, [sp]            // store w8 to memory
    ld1d     { z0.d }, p0/z, [sp]       // load into Z0 (with predicate p0/z)
    addvl    sp, sp, #1          // adjust sp by one vector–length

    // --- Load constant2 (250 in x10) into vector register Z1.
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x10, [sp]
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    // --- Load computed multiplier (x9) into vector register Z2.
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x9, [sp]
    ld1d     { z2.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    // Use movprfx as a hint to combine with the mls instruction.
    movprfx z0.d, p0/m, z0.d
    // mls (indexed): Z0 = Z0 - ( Z2 * (element from Z1 selected by immediate index 0) )
    mls      z0.d, z2.d, z1.d[0]

    // Move the result back from vector (first element) to w0.
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    st1d     { z0.d }, p0, [sp, #0]
    ldr      w0, [sp, #0]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    b        powm_epilogue

powm_odd:
    // ODD exponent branch.
    sub    w1, w1, #1
    mov    w0, w19
    bl     powm

    mov    w8, #19923
    movk   w8, #4194, lsl #16
    mul    w9, w0, w19
    smull  x8, w9, w8
    lsr    x10, x8, #63
    asr    x8, x8, #36
    mov    w10, #250
    add    w8, w8, w10

    // Use SVE mls (indexed) to compute: result = w8 - (x10 * ?)
    ptrue    p0.d
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x9, [sp]            // store one multiplier operand (x9)
    ld1d     { z0.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x10, [sp]           // store the other multiplier (x10)
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x8, [sp]            // store w8 into vector register Z2.
    ld1d     { z2.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    movprfx z2.d, p0/m, z2.d
    mls      z2.d, z1.d, z0.d[0]
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    st1d     { z2.d }, p0, [sp, #0]
    ldr      w0, [sp, #0]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

powm_epilogue:
    ldp    x19, xzr, [sp], #16   // restore saved x19
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #32
    ret

powm_base:
    mov    w0, #1
    ret

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Function: main
// Sets up a local memory buffer, performs a vectorized memset,
// a vectorized memcpy, and then runs an inner loop that uses index, lsl,
// mls, etc. Finally it calls printf to print a computed result.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    .global main
    .type main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: save frame pointer and callee–saved registers.
    stp    x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
    mov    x29, sp
    stp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    stp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    stp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    stp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    stp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]

    // Reserve 4000 bytes on the stack.
    sub    sp, sp, #4000

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memset: Fill 2000 bytes (at sp+2000) with zero.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add    x5, sp, #2000      // destination pointer for memset.
    mov    x4, #2000          // byte count.
memset_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    cntd     w7, p0, #1       // count of active 64–bit lanes
    rdvl     x8, #1           // x8 = current vector–length in bytes
    and      z0.d, z0.d, #0x0 // zero the vector register
    st1d     { z0.d }, p0, [x5]   // store the zero vector
    addvl    x5, x5, #1       // advance pointer by one vector–length
    sub      x4, x4, x8       // subtract processed byte count
    cmp      x4, #0
    b.gt     memset_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memcpy: Copy 2000 bytes from sp (source) to sp+2000 (destination).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    mov    x24, sp           // source pointer
    add    x0, sp, #2000     // destination pointer
    mov    x9, #2000         // byte count.
memcpy_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [x24]  // load a full vector from source
    movprfx  z1.d, p0/m, z1.d       // hint to merge operations
    st1d     { z1.d }, p0, [x0]     // store the vector to destination
    addvl    x24, x24, #1
    addvl    x0, x0, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     memcpy_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized inner loop: Process the 2000–byte region.
    // For each vector–chunk we build an index vector, shift it, then use mls.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add   x24, sp, #2000      // source pointer.
    add   x23, sp, #2000      // destination pointer.
    mov   x9, #2000         // byte count.
inner_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1         // get current chunk size in bytes.
    index    z2.d, #0, #8   // build index vector: {0, 8, 16, ...}
    lsl      z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #1   // shift each element left by 1.
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [x24]  // load vector from source.
    movprfx  z1.d, p0/m, z1.d
    mls      z1.d, z2.d, z1.d[0]    // z1 = z1 - (z2 * (z1[0]))
    st1d     { z1.d }, p0, [x23]     // store the processed vector.
    addvl    x24, x24, #1
    addvl    x23, x23, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     inner_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Call printf to print a result.
    // (For demonstration we load the first 64–bit word from the processed region.)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    ldr    x8, [sp, #2000]       // load a result from memory.
    adrp   x0, .L_str
    add    x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    udiv   x9, x8, x21
    msub   x1, x9, x21, x8
    bl     printf

    // Epilogue: restore registers and stack.
    mov    w0, wzr
    add    sp, sp, #4000
    ldp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]
    ldp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    ldp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    ldp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    ldp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #96
    ret

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Constant string for printf.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    .data
    .align 3
.L_str:
    .asciz "%llu\n"

    .global main
    .type main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: save frame pointer and callee–saved registers.
    stp    x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
    mov    x29, sp
    stp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    stp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    stp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    stp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    stp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]

    // Reserve 4000 bytes on the stack.
    sub    sp, sp, #4000

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memset: Fill 2000 bytes (at sp+2000) with zero.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add    x5, sp, #2000      // destination pointer for memset.
    mov    x4, #2000          // byte count.
memset_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    cntd     w7, p0           // Fixed: count of active 64–bit lanes (predicate without “.d”)
    rdvl     x8, #1           // x8 = current vector–length in bytes
    eor      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d // zero the vector register
    st1d     { z0.d }, p0, [x5]
    addvl    x5, x5, #1       // advance pointer by one vector–length
    sub      x4, x4, x8       // subtract processed byte count
    cmp      x4, #0
    b.gt     memset_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memcpy: Copy 2000 bytes from sp (source) to sp+2000 (destination).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    mov    x24, sp           // source pointer
    add    x0, sp, #2000     // destination pointer
    mov    x9, #2000         // byte count.
memcpy_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [x24]
    st1d     { z1.d }, p0, [x0]
    addvl    x24, x24, #1
    addvl    x0, x0, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     memcpy_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized inner loop: Process the 2000–byte region.
    // For each vector–chunk we build an index vector, shift it, then use mls.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add   x24, sp, #2000      // source pointer.
    add   x23, sp, #2000      // destination pointer.
    mov   x9, #2000         // byte count.
inner_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1         // get current chunk size in bytes.
    index    z2.d, #0, #8   // build index vector: {0, 8, 16, ...}
    lsl      z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #1   // shift each element left by 1.
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [x24]

    addvl    x24, x24, #1
    addvl    x23, x23, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     inner_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Call printf to print a result.
    // (For demonstration we load the first 64–bit word from the processed region.)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    ldr    x8, [sp, #2000]       // load a result from memory.
    adrp   x0, .L_str
    add    x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    udiv   x9, x8, x21
    msub   x1, x9, x21, x8
    bl     printf

    // Epilogue: restore registers and stack.
    mov    w0, wzr
    add    sp, sp, #4000
    ldp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]
    ldp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    ldp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    ldp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    ldp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #96
    ret

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Constant string for printf.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    .data
    .align 3
.L_str:
    .asciz "%llu\n"

    cbz    w1, powm_base

    mov    x29, sp
    stp    x19, xzr, [sp, #-16]!   // save x19 (base operand)

    mov    w0, w19            // pass base operand into recursive call
    cinc   w8, w1, lt        // w8 = (w1+1) if condition (used to compute half)
    asr    w1, w8, #1        // w1 = half exponent
    bl     powm              // recursive call; result in w0

    movk   w9, #4194, lsl #16
    // Constant2 = 250

    // Compute: umull x9, w8, w9, then lsr x9, x9, #36.
    umull  x9, w8, w9
    lsr    x9, x9, #36

    // Now compute: result = w8 - (x9 * 250)
    // We “simulate” a multiply–subtract using SVE mls (indexed).
    ptrue    p0.d                // set predicate p0 with 64–bit elements

    // Using a temporary buffer on the stack to move our scalar values
    // --- Load w8 into vector register Z0.
    sub      sp, sp, #16         // allocate 16 bytes
    str      x8, [sp]            // store w8 to memory
    ld1d     { z0.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1          // adjust sp by one vector–length

    // --- Load constant2 (250 in x10) into vector register Z1.
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x10, [sp]
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    // --- Load computed multiplier (x9) into vector register Z2.
    sub      sp, sp, #16
    str      x9, [sp]
    ld1d     { z2.d }, p0/z, [sp]
    addvl    sp, sp, #1

    // Use an (unpredicated) movprfx hint.
    movprfx  z0, z0
    // mls (indexed): Z0 = Z0 - (Z2 * (element from Z1 selected by immediate index 0))
    mls      z0.d, z2.d, z1.d[0]

// a vectorized memcpy, and then runs an inner loop using index, lsl,
// mls, etc. Finally it calls printf to print a computed result.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    .global main
    .type main, @function
main:
    // Prologue: save frame pointer and callee–saved registers.
    stp    x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
    mov    x29, sp
    stp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    stp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    stp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    stp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    stp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]

    // Reserve 4000 bytes on the stack.
    sub    sp, sp, #4000

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memset: Fill 2000 bytes (at sp+2000) with zero.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add    x5, sp, #2000      // destination pointer for memset.
    mov    x4, #2000          // byte count.

    ptrue    p0.d
    // Use CNTD with immediate #8 so that (number of active 64–bit lanes)*8 yields the byte count.
    cntd     w7, p0, #8       
    uxtw     x8, w7           // extend to 64–bits: now x8==VL in bytes.
    eor      z0.d, z0.d, z0.d // zero the vector register
    st1d     { z0.d }, p0, [x5]
    addvl    x5, x5, #1       // advance pointer by one vector–length
    sub      x4, x4, x8       // subtract processed byte count
    cmp      x4, #0
    b.gt     memset_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized memcpy: Copy 2000 bytes from sp (source) to sp+2000 (destination).
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    mov    x24, sp           // source pointer
    add    x0, sp, #2000     // destination pointer
    mov    x9, #2000         // byte count.

    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1           // x8 = current vector–length in bytes
    ld1d     { z1.d }, p0/z, [x24]
    st1d     { z1.d }, p0, [x0]
    addvl    x24, x24, #1
    addvl    x0, x0, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     memcpy_loop

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Vectorized inner loop: Process the 2000–byte region.
    // For each vector–chunk we build an index vector, shift it, then use mls.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    add   x24, sp, #2000      // source pointer.
    add   x23, sp, #2000      // destination pointer.
    mov   x9, #2000         // byte count.
inner_loop:
    ptrue    p0.d
    rdvl     x8, #1         // current chunk size in bytes.
    index    z2.d, #0, #8   // build index vector: {0, 8, 16, ...}
    lsl      z2.d, p0/m, z2.d, #1   // shift each element left by 1.

    mls      z1.d, z2.d, z1.d[0]
    st1d     { z1.d }, p0, [x23]

    addvl    x23, x23, #1
    sub      x9, x9, x8
    cmp      x9, #0
    b.gt     inner_loop

    // Call printf to print a result.
    // (For demonstration we load the first 64–bit word from the processed region.)
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    add    x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
    udiv   x9, x8, x21
    msub   x1, x9, x21, x8
    bl     printf

    mov    w0, wzr
    add    sp, sp, #4000
    ldp    x20, x19, [sp, #80]
    ldp    x22, x21, [sp, #64]
    ldp    x24, x23, [sp, #48]
    ldp    x26, x25, [sp, #32]
    ldp    x28, x27, [sp, #16]
    ldp    x29, x30, [sp], #96
    ret

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Constant string for printf.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    .data
    .align 3

    .asciz "%llu\n"

	ptrue   p0.s

	/* Use cntw and cnth to count the active lanes (multiplied by immediate 1) */
	cntw    w10, p0, #1      // w10 = count of 32‐bit lanes
	cnth    w11, p0, #1      // w11 = count of 16‐bit lanes

	/* Create a vector of consecutive integers: z0.s := {0, 1, 2, …} */
	index   z0.s, #0, #1

	/* Duplicate the constant 4 into z1 */
	dup     z1.s, #4

	/* Compute vector “square”: z2.s = z0.s * z0.s

	     does: z2.s = 0 + (z0.s * z0.s)

	dup     z2.s, #0

	/* Compute vector “minus index” into z3: z3.s = –z0.s */
	neg     z3.s, p0/m, z0.s

	movprfx z4.s, p0/m, z3.s

	mad     z4.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s

	/* Standard frame setup */
	stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov     x29, sp

	/* Set predicate p0 for 32‐bit (s) elements (all lanes active) */
	ptrue   p0.s

	/* Use cntw and cnth to count the active lanes (multiplied by immediate 1) */
	/* Note: we must indicate the element‐size of the predicate */
	cntw    w10, p0.s, #1      // w10 = count of 32‐bit lanes
	cnth    w11, p0.h, #1      // w11 = count of 16‐bit lanes

	/* Create a vector of consecutive integers: z0.s := {0, 1, 2, …} */
	index   z0.s, #0, #1

	/* Duplicate the constant 4 into z1 */
	dup     z1.s, #4

	/* Compute vector “square”: z2.s = z0.s * z0.s 
	   – initialize accumulator to 0 then use mad:
	     mad  <dest>.<T>, <Pg>/M, <Zn>.<T>, <Za>.<T>
	     does: z2.s = 0 + (z0.s * z0.s)
	*/
	dup     z2.s, #0
	mad     z2.s, p0/m, z0.s, z0.s

	/* Compute vector “minus index” into z3: z3.s = –z0.s */
	neg     z3.s, p0/m, z0.s

	/* Use movprfx to “copy‐merge” the negated vector into z4 */
	movprfx z4.s, p0/m, z3.s
	/* Now do a multiply–add so that:
	     z4.s = (–z0.s) + (z0.s * z1.s) = –z0 + 4*z0 = 3*z0
	*/
	mad     z4.s, p0/m, z0.s, z1.s

	/* Horizontally add (reduce) the two vectors:
	   – uaddv <Dd>, <Pg>, <Zn>.<T> reduces the vector “unsigned‐add” across active lanes.
	*/
	uaddv   d5, p0, z2.s    // d5 = sum of i² terms
	uaddv   d6, p0, z4.s    // d6 = sum of 3×i terms

	/* Transfer reduction results from the SIMD&FP register to general purpose registers.
	   Since uaddv writes a 64–bit result (in a “d” register) we must use fmov to an x register.
	*/
	fmov    x5, d5
	fmov    x6, d6
	add     x7, x5, x6      // x7 = (sum of squares) + (sum of 3×i)

	/* Add in the lane–counts (the result of cntw and cnth are available in w10 and w11,
	   which are just the lower 32 bits of x10 and x11).
	*/
	add     x7, x7, x10     // add count-of-32‐bit lanes
	add     x7, x7, x11     // add count-of-16‐bit lanes

	   after the format string.
	   (The format string is placed in the .rodata section below.)
	   Here we move the lower 32–bits (w7) of x7 into w1.
	*/
	mov     w1, w7
	adr     x0, .L_str
	bl      printf

	/* Return 0 */
	mov     w0, wzr
	ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret
	.size main, .-main

	.section .rodata
	.align 3
