.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global  main
        .type   main, %function

/* 
   This SVE version loads a long string (from .Lnum_str) and “processes” it 
   in chunks. In each iteration the code:
     – builds a byte‐predicate with whilels,
     – loads bytes with ld1b,
     – shifts and masks the bytes (lsr and and),
     – reverses the predicate order (rev),
     – “splices” together two vectors using the destructive form of splice (we backup z1 in z3),
     – extracts (ext) a rotated sub‐vector (using the destructive form via a copy into z4),
     – extracts the last active element with lastb,
     – uses cntw (earlier) and cnth (here) to count how many elements were processed,
     – and advances the pointer.
   Finally the accumulated value is printed.
*/

main:
        // Prologue: allocate 128 bytes and save frame pointer and link register.
        sub     sp, sp, #128
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     x29, sp, #112

        // Set up SVE predicate p0 (all lanes active for 32‐bit elements)
        ptrue   p0.s

        // rdvl returns the current vector length in bytes. (Using #1 gives raw VL.)
        rdvl    x1, #1

        // Count (in 32‐bit “words”) using cntw.
        cntw    x2, ALL         // “ALL” is a built–in predicate constraint.

        // Prepare an index vector in z0.s starting at 0 with increment = 1.
        index   z0.s, #0, #1

        // Load pointer to the number string.
        adrp    x5, .Lnum_str
        add     x5, x5, :lo12:.Lnum_str

        // Load pointer to the "%u\n" format string.
        adrp    x6, .Lformat
        add     x6, x6, :lo12:.Lformat

        // Initialize our accumulator to zero.
        mov     x3, #0

        // x7 holds our current offset; x8 is the string length (1000 bytes).
        mov     x7, #0
        mov     x8, #1000

.Loop:
        cmp     x7, x8
        b.ge    .AfterLoop

        // Build a predicate (p1) for each byte‐element [x7, x8).
        whilels p1.b, x7, x8

        // Load (up to) one vector of bytes from [x5 + x7]
        ld1b    { z1.b }, p1/z, [x5, x7]

        // Shift right each active byte by 1.
        lsr     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #1

        // Mask out all but the low 4 bits.
        and     z1.b, z1.b, #0x0F

        // Reverse the order of the predicate p1 into p2.
        rev     p2.b, p1.b

        // For fun, splice together our modified vector (z1) with the index vector (z0)
        // Note: In base SVE splice is destructive so the destination must equal the first source.
        // Therefore we first copy z1 into z3 to save its original contents.
        mov     z3.b, z1.b
        splice  z1.b, p1, z1.b, z0.b

        // Extract from the splice result a vector that is “rotated” by 8 bytes.
        // (For ext the destructive form requires the destination to equal the first operand.)
        mov     z4.b, z1.b
        ext     z4.b, z4.b, z3.b, #8

        // Extract the last active byte from z1 (zero–extended to 64 bits).
        lastb   x9, p1, z1

        // Accumulate the extracted value.
        add     x3, x3, x9

        // Count the number of active (byte–sized) elements in p1.
        cnth    x10, p1.h

        // Advance the offset by the number of processed elements.
        add     x7, x7, x10
        b       .Loop

.AfterLoop:
        // Now x3 holds our accumulated value.
        // (Force another SVE transfer as a demo.)
        mov     x0, x6
        umov    w1, z0, #15
        mov     w1, w3          // Use the lower word of x3.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate stack space.
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     sp, sp, #128
        mov     x0, #0
        ret

        .align 3

.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global  main
        .type   main, %function

/* 
   This version loads a long number string and “processes” it in chunks. In each iteration,
   it:
     – builds a byte‐predicate with whilels,
     – loads bytes with ld1b,
     – shifts and masks them (lsr and and),
     – reverses the predicate order (rev),
     – “splices” together two vectors using the destructive form of splice (we back up z1 into z3),
     – uses ext to extract a rotated sub‐vector,
     – extracts (lastb) the last active element,
     – uses cntw (earlier) and CNTB (here) to count how many elements were processed,
     – and advances the pointer.
   Finally the accumulated value is printed.
*/

main:
        // Prologue: allocate 128 bytes and save frame pointer and link register.
        sub     sp, sp, #128
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     x29, sp, #112

        // Set up SVE predicate p0 (all lanes active for 32–bit elements)
        ptrue   p0.s

        // rdvl returns the current vector length in bytes. (Using #1 gives raw VL.)
        rdvl    x1, #1

        // Count (in 32‐bit “words”) using cntw.
        cntw    x2, ALL         // “ALL” is a built–in predicate constraint.

        // Prepare an index vector in z0.s starting at 0 with increment = 1.
        index   z0.s, #0, #1

        // Load pointer to our number string.
        adrp    x5, .Lnum_str
        add     x5, x5, :lo12:.Lnum_str

        // Load pointer to the "%u\n" format string.
        adrp    x6, .Lformat
        add     x6, x6, :lo12:.Lformat

        // Initialize our accumulator to zero.
        mov     x3, #0

        // x7 holds our current offset; x8 is the string length (1000 bytes).
        mov     x7, #0
        mov     x8, #1000

.Loop:
        cmp     x7, x8
        b.ge    .AfterLoop

        // Build a predicate (p1) for each byte‐element in [x7, x8).
        whilels p1.b, x7, x8

        // Load (up to) one vector of bytes from [x5 + x7]
        ld1b    { z1.b }, p1/z, [x5, x7]

        // Shift every active byte right by 1.
        lsr     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #1

        // Mask out all but the low 4 bits.
        and     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #0x0F

        // Reverse the order of the predicate p1 into p2.
        rev     p2.b, p1.b

        // For fun, splice together our modified vector (z1) with the index vector (z0).
        // Note: In base SVE splice is destructive so the destination must equal the first source.
        // Therefore we first copy z1 into z3.
        mov     z3, z1
        splice  z1.b, p1, z1.b, z0.b

        // Extract from the splice result a vector that is “rotated” by 8 bytes.
        // (For ext the destructive form requires the destination to equal the first operand.)
        mov     z4, z1
        ext     z4.b, z4.b, z3.b, #8

        // Extract the last active byte from z1 (zero–extended to 64 bits).
        lastb   x9, p1, z1.b

        // Accumulate the extracted value.
        add     x3, x3, x9

        // Count the number of active (byte–sized) elements in p1.
        cntb    x10, p1.b

        // Advance the offset by the number of processed bytes.
        add     x7, x7, x10
        b       .Loop

.AfterLoop:
        // Now x3 holds our accumulated value.
        // (Force another SVE transfer as a demo.)
        mov     x0, x6          // x6 holds our format string pointer.
        umov    w1, z0.s[15]    // Extract element 15 from z0 (SVE->GPR transfer).
        mov     w1, w3          // Use the lower word of x3.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate stack space.
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     sp, sp, #128
        mov     x0, #0
        ret

        .align 3

samples.tested_code:
.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global  main
        .type   main, %function

/* 
   This version loads a long number-string and “processes” it in chunks. In each iteration:
      – builds a byte‐predicate with whilels,
      – loads bytes with ld1b,
      – shifts and masks them (lsr and and),
      – reverses the predicate order (rev),
      – “splices” together two vectors using the destructive form of splice (we must first copy z1 into z3),
      – uses ext to extract a rotated sub–vector,
      – extracts (lastb) the last active element,
      – uses cntw (earlier) and cntb (here) to count how many elements were processed,
      – and advances the pointer.
   Finally the accumulated value is printed.
*/

main:
        // Prologue: allocate 128 bytes and save frame pointer and link register.
        sub     sp, sp, #128
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     x29, sp, #112

        // Set up an SVE predicate p0 (all lanes active for 32–bit elements)
        ptrue   p0.s

        // rdvl returns the current vector length in bytes. (Using #1 gives raw VL.)
        rdvl    x1, #1

        // Count (in 32‐bit “words”) using cntw.
        cntw    x2, ALL         // "ALL" is a built–in predicate constraint.

        // Prepare an index vector in z0.s starting at 0 with increment = 1.
        index   z0.s, #0, #1

        // Load pointer to our number string.
        adrp    x5, .Lnum_str
        add     x5, x5, :lo12:.Lnum_str

        // Load pointer to the "%u\n" format string.
        adrp    x6, .Lformat
        add     x6, x6, :lo12:.Lformat

        // Initialize our accumulator to zero.
        mov     x3, #0

        // x7 holds our current offset; x8 is the string length (1000 bytes).
        mov     x7, #0
        mov     x8, #1000

.Loop:
        cmp     x7, x8
        b.ge    .AfterLoop

        // Build a predicate (p1) for each byte‐element in [x7, x8).
        whilels p1.b, x7, x8

        // Load (up to) one vector of bytes from [x5 + x7]
        ld1b    { z1.b }, p1/z, [x5, x7]

        // Shift every active byte right by 1.
        lsr     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #1

        // Mask out all but the low 4 bits.
        and     z1.b, z1.b, #0x0F

        // Reverse the order of the predicate p1 into p2.
        rev     p2.b, p1.b

        // For fun, splice together our modified vector (z1) with the index vector (z0).
        // Note: In base SVE splice is destructive so the destination must equal the first source.
        // Therefore we first copy z1 (using the “.b” form) into z3.
        mov     z3.b, z1.b
        splice  z1.b, p1, z1.b, z0.b

        // Extract from the splice result a vector that is “rotated” by 8 bytes.
        // (For ext the destructive form requires the destination to equal the first operand.)
        mov     z4.b, z1.b
        ext     z4.b, z4.b, z3.b, #8

        // Extract the last active byte from z1 (zero-extended to 64 bits).
        lastb   x9, p1, z1

        // Accumulate the extracted value.
        add     x3, x3, x9

        // Count the number of active (byte–sized) elements in p1.
        cntb    x10, p1

        // Advance the offset by the number of processed bytes.
        add     x7, x7, x10
        b       .Loop

.AfterLoop:
        // Now x3 holds our accumulated value.
        // (Force another SVE transfer as a demo.)
        mov     x0, x6          // x6 holds our format string pointer.
        umov    w1, z0.s, #15    // Extract element 15 from z0 (SVE-to-GPR transfer).
        mov     w1, w3          // Overwrite with the lower word of x3.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate stack space.
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     sp, sp, #128
        mov     x0, #0
        ret

        .align 3

.arch    armv8.2-a+sve
        .text
        .global  main
        .type   main, %function

/* 
   This version loads a long number-string and “processes” it in chunks. In each iteration:
      – builds a byte‐predicate with whilels,
      – loads bytes with ld1b,
      – shifts and masks them (lsr and and),
      – reverses the predicate order (rev),
      – “splices” together two vectors using the destructive form of splice
         (we must first copy z1 into z3),
      – uses ext to extract a rotated sub–vector,
      – extracts (lastb) the last active element,
      – uses cntw (earlier) and cntb (here) to count how many elements were processed,
      – and advances the pointer.
   Finally the accumulated value is printed.
*/

main:
        // Prologue: allocate 128 bytes and save frame pointer and link register.
        sub     sp, sp, #128
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     x29, sp, #112

        // Set up an SVE predicate p0 (all lanes active for 32–bit elements)
        ptrue   p0.s

        // rdvl returns the current vector length in bytes. (Using #1 gives raw VL.)
        rdvl    x1, #1

        // Count (in 32‐bit “words”) using cntw.
        cntw    x2, ALL         // "ALL" is a built–in predicate constraint.

        // Prepare an index vector in z0.s starting at 0 with increment = 1.
        index   z0.s, #0, #1

        // Load pointer to our number string.
        adrp    x5, .Lnum_str
        add     x5, x5, :lo12:.Lnum_str

        // Load pointer to the "%u\n" format string.
        adrp    x6, .Lformat
        add     x6, x6, :lo12:.Lformat

        // Initialize our accumulator to zero.
        mov     x3, #0

        // x7 holds our current offset; x8 is the string length (1000 bytes).
        mov     x7, #0
        mov     x8, #1000

.Loop:
        cmp     x7, x8
        b.ge    .AfterLoop

        // Build a predicate (p1) for each byte‐element in [x7, x8).
        whilels p1.b, x7, x8

        // Load (up to) one vector of bytes from [x5 + x7]
        ld1b    { z1.b }, p1/z, [x5, x7]

        // Shift every active byte right by 1.
        lsr     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #1

        // Mask out all but the low 4 bits.
        and     z1.b, z1.b, #0x0F

        // Reverse the order of the predicate p1 into p2.
        rev     p2.b, p1.b

        // For fun, splice together our modified vector (z1) with the index vector (z0).
        // Note: In base SVE splice is destructive so the destination must equal the first source.
        // Therefore we first copy z1 into z3.
        mov     z3, z1
        splice  z1.b, p1, z1.b, z0.b

        // Extract from the splice result a vector that is “rotated” by 8 bytes.
        // (For ext the destructive form requires the destination to equal the first operand.)
        mov     z4, z1
        ext     z4.b, z4.b, z3.b, #8

        // Extract the last active byte from z1 (zero-extended to 64 bits).
        lastb   x9, p1, z1.b

        // Accumulate the extracted value.
        add     x3, x3, x9

        // Count the number of active (byte–sized) elements in p1.
        cntb    x10, p1.b

        // Advance the offset by the number of processed bytes.
        add     x7, x7, x10
        b       .Loop

.AfterLoop:
        // Now x3 holds our accumulated value.
        // (Force another SVE transfer as a demo.)
        mov     x0, x6          // x6 holds our format string pointer.
        umov    w1, z0.s[15]    // Extract element 15 from z0 (SVE-to-GPR transfer).
        mov     w1, w3          // Overwrite with the lower word of x3.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate stack space.
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     sp, sp, #128
        mov     x0, #0
        ret

        .align 3

.text
        .global  main
        .type   main, %function

/* 
   This version loads a long number‐string and “processes” it in chunks. In each iteration:
      – builds a byte‐predicate with whilels,
      – loads bytes with ld1b,
      – shifts and masks them (lsr and and),
      – reverses the predicate order (rev),
      – “splices” together two vectors using the destructive form of splice
         (we must first copy z1 into z3 using movprfx),
      – uses ext to extract a rotated sub–vector,
      – extracts (lastb) the last active element,
      – uses cntw (earlier) and cntb (here) to count how many elements were processed,
      – and advances the pointer.
   Finally the accumulated value is printed.
*/

main:
        // Prologue: allocate 128 bytes and save frame pointer and link register.
        sub     sp, sp, #128
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     x29, sp, #112

        // Set up an SVE predicate p0 (all lanes active for 32–bit elements)
        ptrue   p0.s

        // rdvl returns the current vector length in bytes. (Using #1 gives raw VL.)
        rdvl    x1, #1

        // Count (in 32‐bit “words”) using cntw.
        cntw    x2, ALL         // "ALL" is a built–in predicate constraint.

        // Prepare an index vector in z0.s starting at 0 with increment = 1.
        index   z0.s, #0, #1

        // Load pointer to our number string.
        adrp    x5, .Lnum_str
        add     x5, x5, :lo12:.Lnum_str

        // Load pointer to the "%u\n" format string.
        adrp    x6, .Lformat
        add     x6, x6, :lo12:.Lformat

        // Initialize our accumulator to zero.
        mov     x3, #0

        // x7 holds our current offset; x8 is the string length (1000 bytes).
        mov     x7, #0
        mov     x8, #1000

.Loop:
        cmp     x7, x8
        b.ge    .AfterLoop

        // Build a predicate (p1) for each byte‐element in [x7, x8).
        whilels p1.b, x7, x8

        // Load (up to) one vector of bytes from [x5 + x7]
        ld1b    { z1.b }, p1/z, [x5, x7]

        // Shift every active byte right by 1.
        lsr     z1.b, p1/m, z1.b, #1

        // Mask out all but the low 4 bits.
        and     z1.b, z1.b, #0x0F

        // Reverse the order of the predicate p1 into p2.
        rev     p2.b, p1.b

        // For fun, splice together our modified vector (z1) with the index vector (z0).
        // Note: In base SVE splice is destructive so the destination must equal the first source.
        // Therefore we first copy z1 into z3.
        movprfx z3, z1
        splice  z1.b, p1, z1.b, z0.b

        // Extract from the splice result a vector that is “rotated” by 8 bytes.
        // (For ext the destructive form requires the destination to equal the first operand.)
        movprfx z4, z1
        ext     z4.b, z4.b, z3.b, #8

        // Extract the last active byte from z1 (zero–extended to 64 bits).
        lastb   x9, p1, z1

        // Accumulate the extracted value.
        add     x3, x3, x9

        // Count the number of active (byte–sized) elements in p1.
        cntb    x10, p1

        // Advance the offset by the number of processed bytes.
        add     x7, x7, x10
        b       .Loop

.AfterLoop:
        // Now x3 holds our accumulated value.
        // (Force another SVE transfer as a demo.)
        mov     x0, x6          // x6 holds our format string pointer.
        umov    w1, z0.s, #15   // Extract element 15 from z0 (SVE-to-GPR transfer).
        mov     w1, w3          // Overwrite with the lower word of x3.
        bl      printf

        // Epilogue: restore registers and deallocate stack space.
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp, #112]
        add     sp, sp, #128
        mov     x0, #0
        ret

        .align 3

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.global main
	.align 2
	.type main, %function
main:
	// Create a standard frame.
	stp	 x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov	 x29, sp

	// --- Set up SVE predicates and do some SVE “setup” ---
	// ptrue creates an all‐active predicate.
	ptrue	p0.s		// p0: all lanes active for word operations
	ptrue	p1.b		// p1: all lanes active for byte operations

	// Use RDVL to read a multiple of the current SVE vector length (in bytes).
	// (Use immediate #31 because valid immediates are in the range –32 to 31.)
	rdvl	x0, #31		// (for demonstration; x0 now is set to 31×VL bytes)

	// Create an index vector.
	index	z0.s, #0, #1	// z0.s = {0, 1, 2, …}

	// Initialize maximum product (in w5) and loop counter (x10).
	mov	   w5, #0		// max product so far = 0
	mov	   x10, #0		// outer loop index = 0
	mov	   x1, #1000	// total length of our digit string

Loop:
	cmp	 x10, x1
	b.ge	 EndLoop	// if index reached/exceeded length, exit

	// Compute pointer (x11) to digits[x10]. (Reload base pointer each iteration.)
	adrp	x9, .Ldigits
	add	 x9, x9, :lo12:.Ldigits
	add	 x11, x9, x10

	// Use SVE’s whilels to generate a predicate for the “remaining” digits.
	whilels	p2.s, x10, x1

	// Load the digits (as bytes) into z1 using ld1b.
	ld1b	{z1.b}, p2/z, [x11]

	// Convert the loaded ASCII digits to values (digit = (ascii & 0xf)).
	and	 z1.b, z1.b, #0xf

	// --- Use additional SVE instructions (their results here are “dummy” but required) ---
	rev	 p3.b, p1.b		// Reverse all elements in predicate p1 -> p3.
	// Supply the required immediate for cntw and cnth.
	cntw	 w10, p1.s, #1		// Count (in words) active elements in p1.
	cnth	 w11, p1.h, #1		// Count (in halfwords) active in p1.

	// For LSR (logical shift right) the result is written destructively,
	// so first copy z1 into z4 and then shift z4 in place.
	mov	 z4, z1
	lsr	 z4.s, p0/m, z4.s, #1	// Shift right each 32‐bit element by 1.

	// The splice instruction is destructive: the destination must equal the first source.
	// Here we copy z1 into z2 and splice z2 with z1.
	mov	 z2, z1
	splice	 z2.b, p0, z2.b, z1.b	// Splice two vectors (here z2 with z1).

	// lastb extracts the “last” active element (this one is not destructive).
	lastb	 w9, p0, z1.b		// Extract last element from z1 (under full p0).

	// Similarly, EXT is destructive – copy z1 to z3 then use EXT.
	mov	 z3, z1
	ext	 z3.b, z3.b, z1.b, #1	// Extract a shifted vector (shifted by 1 byte).

	// --- Compute the product for the 13‑digit window starting at x10. 
	// (We do this “scalar‐style” – note that a real vectorized solution might reduce the inner loop.)
	mov	 w2, #1		// product accumulator = 1
	mov	 x3, #0		// inner loop index = 0

MulLoop:
	cmp	 x3, #13
	b.ge	 MulDone
	ldrb	 w4, [x11, x3]	// Load one ASCII digit.
	sub	 w4, w4, #48		// Convert from ASCII ('0'=48) to digit.
	mul	 w2, w2, w4		// Multiply into the accumulator.
	add	 x3, x3, #1
	b	 MulLoop

MulDone:
	// Update the maximum product if needed.
	cmp	 w2, w5
	b.lt	 SkipUpdate
	mov	 w5, w2
SkipUpdate:
	// Increment outer loop index.
	add	 x10, x10, #1
	b	 Loop

EndLoop:
	// --- Print the result using printf (assumes libc is linked) ---
	adrp	 x0, .Lformat
	add	 x0, x0, :lo12:.Lformat
	mov	 w1, w5
	bl	 printf

	mov	 w0, #0
	ldp	 x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

	// --- Data sections ---
	.align	3
	.type	.Ldigits, %object
.Ldigits:
	.asciz ""
	.size	.Ldigits, .- .Ldigits

	.align	3
	.type	.Lformat, %object
.Lformat:
	.asciz "%u\n"
	.size	.Lformat, .- .Lformat

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
	.text
	.global main
	.align 2
	.type main, %function
main:
	// Create a standard frame.
	stp	 x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
	mov	 x29, sp

	// --- Set up SVE predicates and do some SVE “setup” ---
	// ptrue creates an all‐active predicate.
	ptrue	p0.s		// p0: all lanes active for word operations
	ptrue	p1.b		// p1: all lanes active for byte operations
	ptrue	p4.h		// p4: all lanes active for halfword operations

	// Use RDVL to read a multiple of the current SVE vector length (in bytes).
	// (We use immediate #31 because valid immediates are in the range –32 to 31.)
	rdvl	x0, #31		// (x0 = 31×VL bytes)

	// Create an index vector.
	index	z0.s, #0, #1	// z0.s = {0, 1, 2, …}

	// Initialize maximum product (in w5) and loop counter (x10).
	mov	   w5, #0		// max product so far = 0
	mov	   x10, #0		// outer loop index = 0
	mov	   x1, #1000	// total length of our digit string

Loop:
	cmp	 x10, x1
	b.ge	 EndLoop	// if index reached/exceeded length, exit

	// Compute pointer (x11) to digits[x10]. (Reload base pointer each iteration.)
	adrp	x9, .Ldigits
	add	 x9, x9, :lo12:.Ldigits
	add	 x11, x9, x10

	// Use SVE’s whilels to generate a predicate for the “remaining” digits.
	whilels	p2.s, x10, x1

	// Load the digits (as bytes) into z1 using ld1b.
	ld1b	{z1.b}, p2/z, [x11]

	// Convert the loaded ASCII digits to values (digit = (ascii & 0xf)).
	and	 z1.b, z1.b, #0xf

	// --- Use additional SVE instructions (their results here are “dummy” but required) ---
	rev	 p3.b, p1.b		// Reverse all elements in predicate p1 -> p3.
	// Supply the required immediate for cntw and cnth.
	cntw	 w10, p0.s, #1		// Count (in words) active elements in p0.
	cnth	 w11, p4.h, #1		// Count (in halfwords) active in p4.

	// For LSR (logical shift right) the result is written destructively,
	// so first copy z1 into z4 and then shift z4 in place.
	movprfx	 z4, z1
	lsr	 z4.s, p0/m, z4.s, #1	// Shift right each 32‐bit element by 1.

	// The splice instruction is destructive: the destination must equal the first source.
	// Here we copy z1 into z2 and splice z2 with z1.
	movprfx	 z2, z1
	splice	 z2.b, p0, z2.b, z1.b	// Splice two vectors (here z2 with z1).

	// lastb extracts the “last” active element (this one is not destructive).
	lastb	 w9, p0, z1.b		// Extract last element from z1 (under full p0).

	// Similarly, EXT is destructive – copy z1 to z3 then use EXT.
	movprfx	 z3, z1
	ext	 z3.b, z3.b, z1.b, #1	// Extract a shifted vector (shifted by 1 byte).

	// --- Compute the product for the 13‑digit window starting at x10. 
	// (This “scalar‐style” inner loop is for demonstration only.)
	mov	 w2, #1		// product accumulator = 1
	mov	 x3, #0		// inner loop index = 0

MulLoop:
	cmp	 x3, #13
	b.ge	 MulDone
	ldrb	 w4, [x11, x3]	// Load one ASCII digit.
	sub	 w4, w4, #48		// Convert from ASCII ('0'=48) to digit.
	mul	 w2, w2, w4		// Multiply into the accumulator.
	add	 x3, x3, #1
	b	 MulLoop

MulDone:
	// Update the maximum product if needed.
	cmp	 w2, w5
	b.lt	 SkipUpdate
	mov	 w5, w2
SkipUpdate:
	// Increment outer loop index.
	add	 x10, x10, #1
	b	 Loop

EndLoop:
	// --- Print the result using printf (assumes libc is linked) ---
	adrp	 x0, .Lformat
	add	 x0, x0, :lo12:.Lformat
	mov	 w1, w5
	bl	 printf

	mov	 w0, #0
	ldp	 x29, x30, [sp], #16
	ret

	// --- Data sections ---
	.align	3
	.type	.Ldigits, %object
.Ldigits:
	.asciz ""
	.size	.Ldigits, .- .Ldigits

	.align	3
	.type	.Lformat, %object
.Lformat:
	.asciz "%u\n"
	.size	.Lformat, .- .Lformat

.text
    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!      // Save FP and LR
    mov     x29, sp
    sub     sp, sp, #4096              // Allocate 4096 bytes of stack

    // Set up “workspace” pointers and constants.
    // (These roughly mimic the original register conventions.)
    mov     x9, sp                   // base pointer for result array (store area)
    sub     x10, x9, #424            // pointer used in our vector reduction branch
    mov     x13, sp                  // pointer used in our scalar reduction branch
    mov     w14, #1                  // initial running value in x14
    mov     x8, xzr                  // initialize counter in x8 = 0
    mov     x1, #1                   // loop index (x1) starts at 1
    mov     w12, #16960              // lower half of threshold (to become 15<<16|16960)
    mov     x11, #-49                // used later in branch tests
    movk    w12, #15, lsl #16        // x12 becomes 15<<16 | 16960 = 1000000

    // Set up SVE predicate for double‐words.
    ptrue   p0.d

    // Get the current SVE vector registration length in bytes.
    rdvl    x20, #1
    // Convert x20 from bytes (VL) to a count of 64‐bit elements.
    lsr     x20, x20, #3

    // Count active 32‐bit elements in p0 (the result is not used but required).
    cntw    w19, p0

//------- Begin main loop -------
Loop:
    // Decide which “inner loop” to execute.
    // For lower loop indices, do a simple update.
    cmp     x1, #51
    b.lt    SimplePart

    // Otherwise choose between vector reduction and “scalar” reduction.
    sub     x16, x8, #49          // compute x16 = (x8 – 49)
    cmp     x16, #4
    b.hs    VectorPart            // if (x8-49) ≥ 4, do vector reduction branch
    b       ScalarPart            // else, take the scalar reduction branch

//------- Vector reduction branch (using ld1d/uaddv) -------
VectorPart:
    // Initialize two SVE accumulators to zero.
    dup     z0.d, xzr             // main accumulator in z0 (use xzr, not wzr)
    dup     z1.d, xzr             // secondary accumulator in z1
    // Align x16 and x11 to a multiple of 4 (per the original code).
    and     x17, x16, #-4
    and     x18, x11, #-4
VectorLoop:
    subs    x18, x18, #4         // decrement loop count (x18 holds number of “chunks”)
    // Load one chunk from memory into z2.
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x10]
    // Load a second chunk (using an offset of x20, now defined as VL/8) into z3.
    ld1d    {z3.d}, p0/z, [x10, x20, LSL #3]
    // Advance the pointer by VL bytes (note: x20 is in 64‐bit elements so LSL #3 multiplies by 8).
    add     x10, x10, x20, LSL #3
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z2.d      // accumulate first vector
    add     z1.d, z1.d, z3.d      // accumulate second vector
    cbnz    x18, VectorLoop
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z1.d      // combine the two accumulators
    // Horizontal unsigned add reduction.
    uaddv   d4, p0, z0.d
    fmov    x14, d4             // move the reduced result into x14
    b       AfterPart

//------- Scalar reduction branch (using rev and ld1d) -------
ScalarPart:
    mov     x15, #50
    neg     x15, x15            // set x15 = -50
ScalarLoop:
    // Reverse order of predicate lanes.
    rev     p1.d, p0.d
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x13, x15, LSL #3]
    // Sum the loaded element(s) with uaddv.
    uaddv   d3, p0, z2.d
    fmov    x16, d3
    add     x14, x14, x16
    sub     x15, x15, #1        // decrement x15
    add     x17, x1, x15        // compute loop‐termination value
    cbnz    x17, ScalarLoop
    b       AfterPart

//------- Simple branch: just update the running value -------
SimplePart:
    add     x14, x14, #1

AfterPart:
    // Store the updated running value into the workspace.
    str     x14, [x9, x1, LSL #3]

    // Check whether the threshold has been reached.
    cmp     x14, x12
    b.ge    ExitLoop

    // Loop‐end update: increment various counters and pointers.
    add     x1, x1, #1         // next iteration index
    add     x8, x8, #1         // bump our “extra” counter
    add     x11, x11, #1       // update x11 as in the original code
    add     x13, x13, #8       // advance the scalar branch pointer by one doubleword
    add     x10, x10, #8       // likewise advance the vector branch pointer by one doubleword
    cmp     x1, #1000
    b.ne    Loop

//------- Exit: call printf when threshold is reached -------
ExitLoop:
    adr     x0, .L_str         // load address of format string
    bl      printf             // call standard printf
    mov     w0, wzr

    // Epilogue: restore stack and return.
    add     sp, sp, #4096
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
    ret

    // Data section for string constant.
    .data
    .align 3
.L_str:
    .asciz "%i\n"

    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!      // Save FP and LR
    mov     x29, sp
    sub     sp, sp, #4096              // Allocate 4096 bytes of stack

    // Set up “workspace” pointers and constants.
    // (These roughly mimic the original register conventions.)
    mov     x9, sp                   // base pointer for result array (store area)
    sub     x10, x9, #424            // pointer used in our vector reduction branch
    mov     x13, sp                  // pointer used in our scalar reduction branch
    mov     w14, #1                  // initial running value in x14
    mov     x8, xzr                  // initialize counter in x8 = 0
    mov     x1, #1                   // loop index (x1) starts at 1
    mov     w12, #16960              // lower half of threshold (to become 15<<16|16960)
    mov     x11, #-49                // used later in branch tests
    movk    w12, #15, lsl #16        // x12 becomes 15<<16 | 16960 = 1000000

    // Set up SVE predicate for double‐words.
    ptrue   p0.d

    // Get the current SVE vector registration length in bytes.
    rdvl    x20, #1
    // Convert x20 from bytes (VL) to a count of 64‐bit elements.
    lsr     x20, x20, #3

    // Count active 32‐bit elements in p0 (the result is not used but required).
    cntw    w19, p0

//------- Begin main loop -------
Loop:
    // Decide which “inner loop” to execute.
    // For lower loop indices, do a simple update.
    cmp     x1, #51
    b.lt    SimplePart

    // Otherwise choose between vector reduction and “scalar” reduction.
    sub     x16, x8, #49          // compute x16 = (x8 – 49)
    cmp     x16, #4
    b.hs    VectorPart            // if (x8-49) ≥ 4, do vector reduction branch
    b       ScalarPart            // else, take the scalar reduction branch

//------- Vector reduction branch (using ld1d/uaddv) -------
VectorPart:
    // Initialize two SVE accumulators to zero.
    dup     z0.d, wzr             // main accumulator in z0
    dup     z1.d, wzr             // secondary accumulator in z1
    // Align x16 and x11 to a multiple of 4 (per the original code).
    and     x17, x16, #-4
    and     x18, x11, #-4
VectorLoop:
    subs    x18, x18, #4         // decrement loop count (x18 holds number of “chunks”)
    // Load one chunk from memory into z2.
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x10]
    // Load a second chunk (using an offset of x20, now defined as VL/8) into z3.
    ld1d    {z3.d}, p0/z, [x10, x20, LSL #3]
    // Advance the pointer by VL bytes (note: x20 is in 64‐bit elements so LSL #3 multiplies by 8).
    add     x10, x10, x20, LSL #3
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z2.d      // accumulate first vector
    add     z1.d, z1.d, z3.d      // accumulate second vector
    cbnz    x18, VectorLoop
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z1.d      // combine the two accumulators
    // Horizontal unsigned add reduction.
    uaddv   d4, p0, z0.d
    fmov    x14, d4             // move the reduced result into x14
    b       AfterPart

//------- Scalar reduction branch (using rev and ld1d) -------
ScalarPart:
    mov     x15, #50
    neg     x15, x15            // set x15 = -50
ScalarLoop:
    // Reverse order of predicate lanes.
    rev     p1.d, p0.d
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x13, x15, LSL #3]
    // Sum the loaded element(s) with uaddv.
    uaddv   d3, p0, z2.d
    fmov    x16, d3
    add     x14, x14, x16
    sub     x15, x15, #1        // decrement x15
    add     x17, x1, x15        // compute loop‐termination value
    cbnz    x17, ScalarLoop
    b       AfterPart

//------- Simple branch: just update the running value -------
SimplePart:
    add     x14, x14, #1

AfterPart:
    // Store the updated running value into the workspace.
    str     x14, [x9, x1, LSL #3]

    // Check whether the threshold has been reached.
    cmp     x14, x12
    b.ge    ExitLoop

    // Loop‐end update: increment various counters and pointers.
    add     x1, x1, #1         // next iteration index
    add     x8, x8, #1         // bump our “extra” counter
    add     x11, x11, #1       // update x11 as in the original code
    add     x13, x13, #8       // advance the scalar branch pointer by one doubleword
    add     x10, x10, #8       // likewise advance the vector branch pointer by one doubleword
    cmp     x1, #1000
    b.ne    Loop

//------- Exit: call printf when threshold is reached -------
ExitLoop:
    adr     x0, .L_str         // load address of format string
    bl      printf             // call standard printf
    mov     w0, wzr

    // Epilogue: restore stack and return.
    add     sp, sp, #4096
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
    ret

    // Data section for string constant.
    .data
    .align 3
.L_str:
    .asciz "%i\n"

    .global main
    .p2align 2
main:
    // Prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!      // save FP and LR
    mov     x29, sp
    sub     sp, sp, #4096              // allocate 4096 bytes of stack

    // Set up “workspace” pointers and constants.
    // (These roughly mimic the original register conventions.)
    mov     x9, sp                   // base pointer for result array (store area)
    sub     x10, x9, #424            // pointer used in our vector reduction branch
    mov     x13, sp                  // pointer used in our scalar reduction branch
    mov     w14, #1                  // initial running value in x14
    mov     x8, xzr                  // initialize counter in x8 = 0
    mov     x1, #1                   // loop index (x1) starts at 1
    mov     w12, #16960              // lower half of threshold (to become 15<<16|16960)
    mov     x11, #-49                // used later in branch tests
    movk    w12, #15, lsl #16        // x12 becomes 15<<16 | 16960 = 1000000

    // Set up SVE predicate.
    ptrue   p0.d

    // Get the current SVE vector registration length in bytes.
    rdvl    x20, #1
    // Convert VL in bytes to a count of 64‐bit elements.
    lsr     x20, x20, #3

    // Count active 32‐bit elements in p0.
    cntw    w19, p0.s

//------- Begin main loop -------
Loop:
    // Decide which “inner loop” to execute.
    // For lower loop indices, do a simple update.
    cmp     x1, #51
    b.lt    SimplePart

    // Otherwise choose between vector reduction and “scalar” reduction.
    sub     x16, x8, #49          // compute x16 = (x8 – 49)
    cmp     x16, #4
    b.hs    VectorPart            // if (x8-49) ≥ 4, do vector reduction branch
    b       ScalarPart            // else, take the scalar reduction branch

//------- Vector reduction branch (using ld1d/uaddv) -------
VectorPart:
    // Clear our accumulator registers.
    mov     x21, xzr
    dup     z0.d, x21             // main accumulator in z0 (set to 0)
    dup     z1.d, x21             // secondary accumulator in z1
    // Align x16 and x11 to a multiple of 4.
    and     x17, x16, #-4
    and     x18, x11, #-4
VectorLoop:
    subs    x18, x18, #4         // decrement loop count (x18 holds number of “chunks”)
    // Load one “chunk” from memory into z2.
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x10]
    // Load a second chunk (using an offset of x20) into z3.
    ld1d    {z3.d}, p0/z, [x10, x20, LSL #3]
    // Advance the pointer by VL bytes.
    add     x10, x10, x20, LSL #3
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z2.d      // accumulate first vector
    add     z1.d, z1.d, z3.d      // accumulate second vector
    cbnz    x18, VectorLoop
    add     z0.d, z0.d, z1.d      // combine the two accumulators
    // Horizontal unsigned add reduction.
    uaddv   d4, p0, z0.d
    fmov    x14, d4             // move the reduced result into x14
    b       AfterPart

//------- Scalar reduction branch (using rev and ld1d) -------
ScalarPart:
    mov     x15, #50
    neg     x15, x15            // set x15 = -50
ScalarLoop:
    // Reverse the order of predicate lanes.
    rev     p1.d, p0.d
    ld1d    {z2.d}, p0/z, [x13, x15, LSL #3]
    // Reduce: sum the loaded element(s).
    uaddv   d3, p0, z2.d
    fmov    x16, d3
    add     x14, x14, x16
    sub     x15, x15, #1        // decrement x15
    add     x17, x1, x15        // compute loop‐termination value
    cbnz    x17, ScalarLoop
    b       AfterPart

//------- Simple branch: just update the running value -------
SimplePart:
    add     x14, x14, #1

AfterPart:
    // Store the updated running value.
    str     x14, [x9, x1, LSL #3]

    // Check whether the threshold has been reached.
    cmp     x14, x12
    b.ge    ExitLoop

    // Loop‐end update: increment various counters and pointers.
    add     x1, x1, #1         // next iteration index
    add     x8, x8, #1         // bump our “extra” counter
    add     x11, x11, #1       // update x11 as in the original code
    add     x13, x13, #8       // advance the scalar branch pointer
    add     x10, x10, #8       // advance the vector branch pointer
    cmp     x1, #1000
    b.ne    Loop

//------- Exit: call printf when threshold is reached -------
ExitLoop:
    adr     x0, .L_str         // load address of format string
    bl      printf             // call standard printf
    mov     w0, wzr

    // Epilogue: restore stack and return.
    add     sp, sp, #4096
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #32
    ret

    // Data section for string constant.
    .data
    .align 3

    .asciz "%i\n"

Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to

• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.global	mult_mod
	.type	mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save original input pointer in x19
	mov		x19, x0

	// Allocate 2592 bytes for the result array.
	mov		w0, #2592
	bl		malloc
	// Save malloc‐returned pointer in x10 (result pointer)
	mov		x10, x0

	// Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.d

	// Use rdvl to read a multiple of VL (demo only).
	rdvl	x0, #1		

	// Get the number of active 64‐bit lanes.
	cntd	x1, #1

	// (Dummy instructions replaced by simple MOVs)
	mov		x11, xzr		// x11 := 0 (dummy)
	mov		x12, xzr		// x12 := 0 (dummy)

	// Loop index: x2 counts the number of 64‐bit elements processed.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_mod_loop:
	cmp		x2, #324
	b.ge	.Lmult_mod_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	//   x11 = x2 * 8, and x12 = x19 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x19, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 2) + 3.
	mov		x8, #3
	dup		z6.d, x8		// z6 := 3
	mov		x7, #2
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 2
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = 3 + (z0 * 2)

	// Now reduce modulo M = 1000000000.
	// Load constant 1000000000. (1000000000 = 0x3B9ACA00)
	movz	x4, #0xCA00		// lower 16 bits
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16	// upper 16 bits
	dup		z1.d, x4		// duplicate into every lane

	// Load the magic constant.
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6

	umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z6.d, z2.d	// high-half( z6 * magic )
	lsr		z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #29	// shift right by 29 bits
	mls		z6.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d	// subtract: z6 = z6 - (z7 * 1000000000)

	// Compute store address: x11 = x2 * 8; x3 = x10 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	// Increment loop index by the vector length.
	add		x2, x2, x1
	b		.Lmult_mod_loop

.Lmult_mod_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
	ret

	.global	mult_vec
	.type	mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save second argument (input pointer) in x20.
	mov		x20, x1

	// Allocate 144 bytes for the result (18 64‐bit elements).
	mov		w0, #144
	bl		malloc
	mov		x10, x0		// result pointer in x10

	// Set up predicate.
	ptrue	p0.d
	cntd	x9, #1

	// Loop index: x2 counts processed elements.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_vec_loop:
	cmp		x2, #18
	b.ge	.Lmult_vec_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x20, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 5) mod 1000000000.
	mov		x7, #5
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 5
	dup		z6.d, xzr		// zero accumulator
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = z0 * 5

	// Reduce modulo 1000000000.
	movz	x4, #0xCA00
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16
	dup		z1.d, x4
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6
	umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z6.d, z2.d
	lsr		z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #29
	mls		z6.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

	// Compute store address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	add		x2, x2, x9
	b		.Lmult_vec_loop

.Lmult_vec_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
	ret

	.global main
	.type main, %function
main:
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
	mov		x29, sp

	// Call calloc(1, 2592) to get an input array.
	mov		w0, #1
	mov		w1, #2592
	bl		calloc
	mov		x19, x0

	// (Assume the calloc‐ed array is already initialized.)

	// Call mult_mod (with both arguments = x19).
	mov		x0, x19
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_mod
	mov		x20, x0

	// Call mult_vec with arguments (mult_mod result, x19)
	mov		x0, x20
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_vec
	mov		x21, x0

	// Load a 64–bit value from the mult_vec array at offset 64.
	ldr		x8, [x21, #64]

	// Prepare to call printf with the format string.
	adrp	x0, .L_str
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	mov		x1, x8
	bl		printf

	mov		w0, #0
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
	ret

	.section .rodata
.L_str:
	.asciz	"%llu\n"

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.global	mult_mod
	.type	mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save original input pointer in x19
	mov		x19, x0

	// Allocate 2592 bytes for the result array.
	mov		w0, #2592
	bl		malloc
	// Save malloc‐returned pointer in x10 (result pointer)
	mov		x10, x0

	// Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.d

	// Use rdvl to read a multiple of VL (demo only).
	rdvl	x0, #1		

	// Get the number of active 64‐bit lanes.
	cntd	x1, #1

	// (Dummy instructions replaced by simple MOVs)
	mov		x11, xzr		// x11 := 0 (dummy)
	mov		x12, xzr		// x12 := 0 (dummy)

	// Loop index: x2 counts the number of 64‐bit elements processed.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_mod_loop:
	cmp		x2, #324
	b.ge	.Lmult_mod_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	//   x11 = x2 * 8, and x12 = x19 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x19, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 2) + 3.
	mov		x8, #3
	dup		z6.d, x8		// z6 := 3
	mov		x7, #2
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 2
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = 3 + (z0 * 2)

	// Now reduce modulo M = 1000000000.
	// Load constant 1000000000. (1000000000 = 0x3B9ACA00)
	movz	x4, #0xCA00		// lower 16 bits
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16	// upper 16 bits
	dup		z1.d, x4		// duplicate into every lane

	// Load the magic constant.
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6

	umulh	z7.d, p0/z, z6.d, z2.d	// high-half( z6 * magic )
	lsr		z7.d, p0/z, z7.d, #29	// shift right by 29 bits
	mls		z6.d, p0/z, z7.d, z1.d	// subtract: z6 = z6 - (z7 * 1000000000)

	// Compute store address: x11 = x2 * 8; x3 = x10 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	// Increment loop index by the vector length.
	add		x2, x2, x1
	b		.Lmult_mod_loop

.Lmult_mod_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
	ret

	.global	mult_vec
	.type	mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save second argument (input pointer) in x20.
	mov		x20, x1

	// Allocate 144 bytes for the result (18 64‐bit elements).
	mov		w0, #144
	bl		malloc
	mov		x10, x0		// result pointer in x10

	// Set up predicate.
	ptrue	p0.d
	cntd	x9, #1

	// Loop index: x2 counts processed elements.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_vec_loop:
	cmp		x2, #18
	b.ge	.Lmult_vec_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x20, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 5) mod 1000000000.
	mov		x7, #5
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 5
	// We cannot use xzr directly here, so use a temporary register.
	mov		x16, xzr		
	dup		z6.d, x16		// z6 := 0 (zero accumulator)
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = z0 * 5

	// Reduce modulo 1000000000.
	movz	x4, #0xCA00
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16
	dup		z1.d, x4
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6
	umulh	z7.d, p0/z, z6.d, z2.d
	lsr		z7.d, p0/z, z7.d, #29
	mls		z6.d, p0/z, z7.d, z1.d

	// Compute store address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	add		x2, x2, x9
	b		.Lmult_vec_loop

.Lmult_vec_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
	ret

	.type	main, %function

	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
	mov		x29, sp

	// Call calloc(1, 2592) to get an input array.
	mov		w0, #1
	mov		w1, #2592
	bl		calloc
	mov		x19, x0

	// (Assume the calloc‐ed array is already initialized.)

	// Call mult_mod (with both arguments = x19).
	mov		x0, x19
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_mod
	mov		x20, x0

	mov		x0, x20
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_vec
	mov		x21, x0

	// Load a 64–bit value from the mult_vec array at offset 64.
	ldr		x8, [x21, #64]

	// Prepare to call printf with the format string.
	adrp	x0, .L_str
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	mov		x1, x8
	bl		printf

	mov		w0, #0
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
	ret

.arch	armv8.2-a+sve
	.text

	.global	mult_mod
	.type	mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save original input pointer in x19
	mov		x19, x0

	// Allocate 2592 bytes for the result array.
	mov		w0, #2592
	bl		malloc
	// Save malloc‐returned pointer in x10 (result pointer)
	mov		x10, x0

	// Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.d

	// Use rdvl to read a multiple of VL (demo only).
	rdvl	x0, #1		

	// Get the number of active 64‐bit lanes.
	cntd	x1, #1

	// (Dummy instructions replaced by simple MOVs)
	mov		x11, xzr		// x11 := 0 (dummy)
	mov		x12, xzr		// x12 := 0 (dummy)

	// Loop index: x2 counts the number of 64‐bit elements processed.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_mod_loop:
	cmp		x2, #324
	b.ge	.Lmult_mod_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	//   x11 = x2 * 8, and x12 = x19 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x19, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 2) + 3.
	mov		x8, #3
	dup		z6.d, x8		// z6 := 3
	mov		x7, #2
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 2
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = 3 + (z0 * 2)

	// Now reduce modulo M = 1000000000.
	// Load constant 1000000000. (1000000000 = 0x3B9ACA00)
	movz	x4, #0xCA00		// lower 16 bits
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16	// upper 16 bits
	dup		z1.d, x4		// duplicate into every lane

	// Load the magic constant.
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6

	// Compute high-half multiplication and shift
	umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z6.d, z2.d	// z7 = high-half(z6 * magic)
	lsr		z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #29	// shift right by 29 bits
	mls		z6.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d	// z6 = z6 - (z7 * 1000000000)

	// Compute store address: x11 = x2 * 8; x3 = x10 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	// Increment loop index by the vector length.
	add		x2, x2, x1
	b		.Lmult_mod_loop

.Lmult_mod_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
	ret

	.global	mult_vec
	.type	mult_vec, %function
mult_vec:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save second argument (input pointer) in x20.
	mov		x20, x1

	// Allocate 144 bytes for the result (18 64‐bit elements).
	mov		w0, #144
	bl		malloc
	mov		x10, x0		// result pointer in x10

	// Set up predicate.
	ptrue	p0.d
	cntd	x9, #1

	// Loop index: x2 counts processed elements.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_vec_loop:
	cmp		x2, #18
	b.ge	.Lmult_vec_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x20, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 5) mod 1000000000.
	mov		x7, #5
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 5
	// We cannot use xzr directly here, so use a temporary register.
	mov		x16, xzr		
	dup		z6.d, x16		// z6 := 0 (zero accumulator)
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = z0 * 5

	// Reduce modulo 1000000000.
	movz	x4, #0xCA00
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16
	dup		z1.d, x4
	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6
	umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z6.d, z2.d
	lsr		z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #29
	mls		z6.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

	// Compute store address:
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x3, x10, x11
	st1d	{ z6.d }, p0, [x3]

	add		x2, x2, x9
	b		.Lmult_vec_loop

.Lmult_vec_end:
	mov		x0, x10
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
	ret

	.global	main
	.type	main, %function
main:
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
	mov		x29, sp

	// Call calloc(1, 2592) to get an input array.
	mov		w0, #1
	mov		w1, #2592
	bl		calloc
	mov		x19, x0

	// (Assume the calloc‐ed array is already initialized.)

	// Call mult_mod (with both arguments = x19).
	mov		x0, x19
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_mod
	mov		x20, x0

	// Call mult_vec with arguments (mult_mod result, x19)
	mov		x0, x20
	mov		x1, x19
	bl		mult_vec
	mov		x21, x0

	// Load a 64–bit value from the mult_vec array at offset 64.
	ldr		x8, [x21, #64]

	// Prepare to call printf with the format string.
	adrp	x0, .L_str
	add		x0, x0, :lo12:.L_str
	mov		x1, x8
	bl		printf

	mov		w0, #0
	ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
	ret

	.section .rodata
.L_str:
	.asciz	"%llu\n"

mult_mod:
	// Function prologue
	stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
	mov		x29, sp
	// Save original input pointer in x19
	mov		x19, x0

	mov		w0, #2592
	bl		malloc
	// Save malloc‐returned pointer in x10 (result pointer)
	mov		x10, x0

	// Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements.
	ptrue	p0.d

	// Use rdvl to read a multiple of VL (demo only).

	// Get the number of active 64‐bit lanes.
	cntd	x1, #1

	// (Dummy instructions replaced by simple MOVs)
	mov		x11, xzr		// x11 := 0 (dummy)
	mov		x12, xzr		// x12 := 0 (dummy)

	// Loop index: x2 counts the number of 64‐bit elements processed.
	mov		x2, xzr

.Lmult_mod_loop:
	cmp		x2, #324
	b.ge	.Lmult_mod_end

	// Compute effective load address:
	//   x11 = x2 * 8, and x12 = x19 + x11.
	lsl		x11, x2, #3
	add		x12, x19, x11
	ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

	// Compute: r = (z0 * 2) + 3.
	mov		x8, #3
	dup		z6.d, x8		// z6 := 3
	mov		x7, #2
	dup		z4.d, x7		// z4 := 2
	mla		z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d	// z6 = 3 + (z0 * 2)

	// Now reduce modulo M = 1000000000.
	// Load constant 1000000000. (1000000000 = 0x3B9ACA00)
	movz	x4, #0xCA00		// lower 16 bits
	movk	x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16	// upper 16 bits
	dup		z1.d, x4		// duplicate into every lane

	ldr		x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
	dup		z2.d, x5
	mov		x6, #29
	dup		z3.d, x6

	//    high(z6*z2) = p3 + (((p1 + p2) + (p0 >> 32)) >> 32)

	//    a = z6, b = z2,
	//    a_lo = a & 0x00000000FFFFFFFF,   a_hi = a >> 32,
	//    b_lo = b & 0x00000000FFFFFFFF,   b_hi = b >> 32,
	//    p0 = a_lo * b_lo,  p1 = a_lo * b_hi,
	//    p2 = a_hi * b_lo,  p3 = a_hi * b_hi.

	// Compute low and high parts of z6 (a)
	and		z8.d, z6.d, #0x00000000FFFFFFFF   // a_lo = z6 & mask
	lsr		z10.d, p0/m, z6.d, #32             // a_hi = z6 >> 32

	add		z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, z17.d
	lsr		z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, #32

        .global mult_mod
        .type   mult_mod, %function
mult_mod:
        // Function prologue
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
        mov     x29, sp
        // Save original input pointer in x19
        mov     x19, x0

        // Allocate 2592 bytes for the result array.
        mov     w0, #2592
        bl      malloc
        // Save malloc‐returned pointer in x10 (result pointer)
        mov     x10, x0

        // Set up SVE predicate for 64‐bit elements.
        ptrue   p0.d

        // Use rdvl to read a multiple of VL (demo only).
        rdvl    x0, #1

        // Get the number of active 64‐bit lanes.
        cntd    x1, #1

        // (Dummy instructions replaced by simple MOVs)
        mov     x11, xzr           // x11 := 0 (dummy)
        mov     x12, xzr           // x12 := 0 (dummy)

        // Loop index: x2 counts the number of 64‐bit elements processed.
        mov     x2, xzr

.Lmult_mod_loop:
        cmp     x2, #324
        b.ge   .Lmult_mod_end

        // Compute effective load address:
        //   x11 = x2 * 8, and x12 = x19 + x11.
        lsl     x11, x2, #3
        add     x12, x19, x11
        ld1d    { z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

        // Compute: r = (z0 * 2) + 3.
        mov     x8, #3
        dup     z6.d, x8         // z6 := 3
        mov     x7, #2
        dup     z4.d, x7         // z4 := 2
        mla     z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d   // z6 = 3 + (z0 * 2)

        // Now reduce modulo M = 1000000000.
        // Load constant 1000000000 (1000000000 = 0x3B9ACA00)
        movz    x4, #0xCA00
        movk    x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16
        dup     z1.d, x4         // z1 := 1000000000

        // Load the magic constant.
        ldr     x5, =0x89705F4136B4A59
        dup     z2.d, x5         // z2 := magic constant
        mov     x6, #29
        dup     z3.d, x6         // z3 := 29

        // -----------------------------------------------------------------
        // Emulate high‐half multiplication:
        //   desired: high(z6*z2) = p3 + (((p1 + p2) + (p0 >> 32)) >> 32)
        //   where:
        //      a = z6, b = z2,
        //      a_lo = a & 0x00000000FFFFFFFF,   a_hi = a >> 32,
        //      b_lo = b & 0x00000000FFFFFFFF,   b_hi = b >> 32,
        //      p0 = a_lo * b_lo,  p1 = a_lo * b_hi,
        //      p2 = a_hi * b_lo,  p3 = a_hi * b_hi.
        //
        // First, compute a_lo and a_hi.
        // Replace “and z8.d, z6.d, #0x00000000FFFFFFFF” by:
        movz    x17, #0xffff, lsl #0       // x17 = lower 16 bits set
        movk    x17, #0xffff, lsl #16      // now x17 = 0x00000000FFFFFFFF
        dup     z20.d, x17                // z20 holds the mask value
        and     z8.d, p0/m, z6.d, z20.d    // a_lo = z6 & mask
        lsr     z10.d, p0/m, z6.d, #32     // a_hi = z6 >> 32

        // Then compute for b.
        movz    x17, #0xffff, lsl #0
        movk    x17, #0xffff, lsl #16
        dup     z21.d, x17                // z21 holds the same mask
        and     z11.d, p0/m, z2.d, z21.d   // b_lo = z2 & mask
        lsr     z12.d, p0/m, z2.d, #32     // b_hi = z2 >> 32

        // Compute the four partial 32–bit multiplications:
        mul     z13.d, p0/m, z8.d, z11.d   // p0 = a_lo * b_lo
        mul     z14.d, p0/m, z8.d, z12.d   // p1 = a_lo * b_hi
        mul     z15.d, p0/m, z10.d, z11.d   // p2 = a_hi * b_lo
        mul     z16.d, p0/m, z10.d, z12.d   // p3 = a_hi * b_hi

        // Compute t = p0 >> 32.
        lsr     z17.d, p0/m, z13.d, #32

        // Compute sum = (p1 + p2) + t, then shift right by 32.
        add     z18.d, p0/m, z14.d, z15.d
        add     z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, z17.d
        lsr     z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, #32

        // Now high(z6*z2) = p3 + (sum)
        add     z7.d, p0/m, z16.d, z18.d

        // Next, do: adjust = high >> 29 and compute:
        lsr     z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, #29
        mls     z6.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d    // z6 = z6 - (z7 * 1000000000)

        // Compute store address: x11 = x2 * 8; x3 = x10 + x11.
        lsl     x11, x2, #3
        add     x3, x10, x11
        st1d    { z6.d }, p0, [x3]

        // Increment loop index by the vector length.
        add     x2, x2, x1

.Lmult_mod_end:
        mov     x0, x10
        ldp     x29, x30, [sp], #96
        ret

mult_vec:

        mov     x29, sp

        mov     x2, xzr

        // Compute effective load address:
        lsl     x11, x2, #3
        add     x12, x20, x11
        ld1d    { z0.d }, p0/z, [x12]

        // Compute: r = (z0 * 5) mod 1000000000.
        mov     x7, #5
        dup     z4.d, x7         // z4 := 5

        mov     x16, xzr
        dup     z6.d, x16        // z6 := 0 (zero accumulator)
        mla     z6.d, p0/m, z0.d, z4.d   // z6 = z0 * 5

        movk    x4, #0x3B9A, lsl #16
        dup     z1.d, x4         // z1 := 1000000000

        mul     z14.d, p0/m, z8.d, z12.d    // p1 = a_lo * b_hi
        mul     z15.d, p0/m, z10.d, z11.d    // p2 = a_hi * b_lo

        add     z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, z17.d
        lsr     z18.d, p0/m, z18.d, #32

        .type   main, %function
main:
        stp     x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
        mov     x29, sp

        // Call calloc(1, 2592) to get an input array.
        mov     w0, #1
        mov     w1, #2592
        bl      calloc
        mov     x19, x0

.align	3
		.text
		.global mult_mod
		.type	mult_mod, %function
/*
  Function: mult_mod 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (for example, to an input “array”)
    x1 = an extra parameter (unused in the example)
  Operation:
    Allocates 0xa20 bytes via malloc; then using SVE it “processes” the input data in vector chunks.
    In each “chunk” it loads a vector of 64‐bit elements (ld1d), then applies a shift left (lsl) and shift right (lsr)
    and a mask (and). Then it multiplies the result by a constant (using mla indexed with [0]) while starting from zero.
    Finally it “reduces modulo” the magic constant (using umulh plus mls) and writes the answer with st1d.
*/
mult_mod:
		// Prologue: save frame pointer and link register
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Save parameter x0 in x19; x1 in x20 (even if unused)
		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 0xa20 (2592) bytes via malloc.
		mov		w0, #2592
		// Set up the “mod constant” in w21: lower half then upper half.
		mov		w21, #51712		        // = 0xCA00
		movk		w21, #15258, lsl #16		// => w21 = 0x3B3ACA00
		bl		malloc			           // result in x0
		// Save the allocated pointer in x24.
		mov		x24, x0

		// (For demonstration, use a SUB immediate – a no–op here.)
		sub		x8, x8, #0

		// Set up SVE predicate covering all 64–bit (dword) elements.
		ptrue	p0.d

		// Obtain the “vector length” in bytes; here rdvl multiplies VL (in bytes) by #8.
		rdvl	x10, #8

		// Count how many 64–bit elements in the predicate.
		cntd	x11, p0, #1

		// Load the mod constant and its reciprocal from memory (each as a “vector constant”).
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0, [x0]		// Each element in z1 = 0x3B3ACA00

		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0, [x0]		// Each element in z2 = reciprocal constant

		// Load a coefficient constant (for multiplying the data) from memory.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0, [x0]		// For example, 2

		// Loop over the allocated block (processing one SVE–vector at a time)
		// x8 holds the current “element–offset” (in number of elements).
mult_mod_loop:
		cmp		x8, #2592
		b.ge		mult_mod_exit

		// Load one vector of 64–bit integers from base x19 with index x8 (×8 converts element–index into byte offset).
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0, [x19, x8, lsl #3]

		// Example use of predicated LSL and LSR: shift left then right.
		lsl		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #1
		lsr		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #1

		// And mask each element to 32–bits.
		and		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #0xFFFFFFFF

		// Zero an accumulator vector by loading a pre–stored zero–vector.
		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate (z4 * constant) into z5.
		// The “mla indexed” uses the 0th element from each 128–bit piece of z3.
		mla		z5.d, p0, z4.d, z3.d[0]

		// Now do a “mod reduction” (compute remainder = z5 – ( (z5×recip) * mod_const ) ).
		umulh	z6.d, p0, z5.d, z2.d		// Vector “quotient” approximation via umulh.
		mls		z5.d, p0, z6.d, z1.d		// Multiply subtract: subtract (quotient * mod) from z5.

		// Write the result vector into the allocated area.
		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		// Increment offset by the number of d–elements processed (in x11).
		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_mod_loop

mult_mod_exit:
		// Return the pointer to the allocated (and filled) block in x0.
		mov		x0, x24

		// Epilogue: restore registers and return.
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
		ret

		.global mult_vec
		.type	mult_vec, %function
/*
  Function: mult_vec 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (for example, to an input data block)
    x1 = a second pointer (used here for addressing a coefficient array)
  Operation:
    Allocates 144 bytes via malloc and then processes the data in a tight SVE vector–loop.
    (Again we use a couple of predicated operations such as LSL, LSR, AND, then MLA and MLS to do
    a “multiply–add” and “mod reduction” computation.)
*/
mult_vec:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Save x0 and x1 for later use.
		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 144 bytes via malloc.
		mov		w0, #144
		mov		w21, #51712
		movk	w21, #15258, lsl #16
		bl		malloc
		mov		x24, x0

		// Set up full predicate and learn the vector–length.
		ptrue	p0.d
		rdvl	x10, #8
		cntd	x11, p0, #1

		// Load coefficient constant for this function.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0, [x0]

		// Loop over 144 bytes (i.e. 144/8 = 18 elements).
		mov		x8, #0
mult_vec_loop:
		cmp		x8, #144
		b.ge		mult_vec_exit

		// Load one vector from the input data block at x20.
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0, [x20, x8, lsl #3]

		// Example predicated shifts and AND.
		lsl		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #2
		lsr		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #2
		and		z4.d, p0, z4.d, #0xFFFF

		// Zero accumulation vector.
		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate product (z4 * constant) into z5.
		mla		z5.d, p0, z4.d, z3.d[0]

		// For a mod–reduction we again load our “mod constant” and reciprocal.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0, [x0]
		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0, [x0]

		umulh	z6.d, p0, z5.d, z2.d
		mls		z5.d, p0, z6.d, z1.d

		// Store result vector.
		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_vec_loop

mult_vec_exit:
		mov		x0, x24
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
		ret

		.global main
		.type	main, %function
/*
  Function: main
  Operation:
    Allocate an initial block (using calloc) and then make several calls to mult_mod and mult_vec.
    Finally a value (loaded with an ordinary ldr) is printed via printf.
*/
main:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Allocate a 2592-byte block with calloc.
		mov		w0, #1
		mov		w1, #2592
		bl		calloc
		mov		x19, x0		// Save pointer in x19

		// For demonstration, store a “1” (via an SVE store) into two chosen offsets.
		// (These addresses mimic the “str” instructions in the original sample.)
		adr		x0, one_const
		ptrue	p0.d
		ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x0]
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x19, #144]
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x19, #1432]

		// Now call mult_mod – pass x19 (the calloc block) as both arguments.
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_mod

		// Then call mult_vec – here for demonstration again pass the pointer.
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_vec

		// Load a 64–bit result from offset 64 (using ordinary ldr) and pass it to printf.
		ldr		x8, [x0, #64]
		adr		x0, fmt_str
		mov		x1, x8
		bl		printf

		mov		w0, wzr
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
		ret

		.data
		.align	3
// mod_const: a full 64–bit constant repeated for every element in a vector.
mod_const:
		.dword	0x000000003B3ACA00

// recip_const: a precomputed “reciprocal” constant (for mod reduction).
		.dword	0x000000000002D79C  // 0x2D79C = 185388 decimal (approximate)

// coeff_const: a coefficient constant (here the value 2)
		.dword	0x0000000000000002

// zero_const: a storage for a zero vector (fill with at least 4 words)
		.dword	0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0

// one_const: a storage for a “one” vector.
		.dword	0x1, 0x1, 0x1, 0x1

// Format string for printf:
fmt_str:
		.asciz	"%llu\n"
		.text

		mov		x29, sp

		mov		x20, x1

		mov		w0, #2592

	.global mult_mod
	.type	mult_mod, %function
/*  
  Function: mult_mod 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (for example, to an input “array”)
    x1 = an extra parameter (unused in the example)
  Operation:
    Allocates 2592 bytes via malloc; then using SVE it “processes” the input data in vector chunks.
    In each chunk it:
      • loads a vector of 64‐bit elements (ld1d with p0/z),
      • shifts left and right (lsl/lsr using p0/m),
      • masks with a 32–bit immediate (and without a predicate),
      • does a multiply–add (mla indexed using p0/m),
      • then does the “mod reduction” (umulh plus mls using p0/m)
    and finally writes the answer (st1d).
*/
mult_mod:
		// Prologue: save frame pointer and link register.
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Save parameters: x0 -> x19 and x1 -> x20.
		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 2592 bytes via malloc.
		mov		w0, #2592
		// Set up the “mod constant” in w21: first lower then upper half.
		mov		w21, #51712		        // 0xCA00
		movk		w21, #15258, lsl #16		// => 0x3B3ACA00
		bl		malloc		           
		mov		x24, x0			// x24 = allocated pointer

		// (For demonstration, a no‐op: subtract 0 from x8.)
		sub		x8, x8, #0

		// Set up predicate for all 64–bit (doubleword) elements.
		ptrue	p0.d

		// Get the current vector length multiplied by 8.
		rdvl	x10, #8

		// Count the number of 64–bit elements in the predicate.
		cntd	x11, p0

		// Load the mod constant and its reciprocal as a “vector constant”.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z1 = mod constant (0x3B3ACA00)

		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z2 = reciprocal constant

		// Load a coefficient constant (for multiplying data) from memory.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// e.g. constant 2

mult_mod_loop:
		cmp		x8, #2592
		b.ge		mult_mod_exit

		// Load one vector (64–bit elements) from [x19, x8, lsl #3].
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0/z, [x19, x8, lsl #3]

		// Shift left then right using the predicate in merge mode.
		lsl		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #1
		lsr		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #1

		// Mask each element to 32–bits; note no predicate is used.
		and		z4.d, z4.d, #0xFFFFFFFF

		// Zero an accumulator vector by loading our zero constant.
		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate (z4 * constant) into z5.
		mla		z5.d, p0/m, z4.d, z3.d, #0

		// Now do mod reduction: we need to compute
		//     result = original_z5 - ( high(original_z5*z2) * z1 )
		// So we copy z5 into a temporary, then use that for the umulh.
		mov		z7.d, z5.d
		umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, z2.d
		mls		z5.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

		// Store the result vector into the allocated block.
		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		// Increment our element–offset by the number of active elements.
		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_mod_loop

mult_mod_exit:
		mov		x0, x24
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
		ret

	.global mult_vec
	.type	mult_vec, %function
/*
  Function: mult_vec 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (to an input data block)
    x1 = pointer (for accessing a coefficient array)
  Operation:
    Allocates 144 bytes via malloc and then processes data in an SVE loop.
    (It loads data, shifts and masks with immediate constants, does a mla and mod reduction via umulh and mls.)
*/
mult_vec:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
		mov		x29, sp

		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 144 bytes.
		mov		w0, #144
		mov		w21, #51712
		movk	w21, #15258, lsl #16
		bl		malloc
		mov		x24, x0

		ptrue	p0.d
		rdvl	x10, #8
		cntd	x11, p0

		// Load coefficient constant.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		mov		x8, #0
mult_vec_loop:
		cmp		x8, #144
		b.ge		mult_vec_exit

		// Load one vector from [x20, x8, lsl #3].
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0/z, [x20, x8, lsl #3]

		// Shift left then right (using immediate #2 now).
		lsl		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #2
		lsr		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #2

		// Mask each element to 16–bits.
		and		z4.d, z4.d, #0xFFFF

		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate (z4 * constant) into z5.
		mla		z5.d, p0/m, z4.d, z3.d, #0

		// For mod–reduction, load the mod constant and its reciprocal.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0/z, [x0]
		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Copy z5 into a temporary, then do mod reduction.
		mov		z7.d, z5.d
		umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, z2.d
		mls		z5.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_vec_loop

mult_vec_exit:
		mov		x0, x24
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
		ret

	.global main
	.type	main, %function
/*
  Function: main
  Operation:
    Allocates a 2592‐byte block with calloc, then (for demo)
    stores the “one” constant at two unusual offsets (using computed addresses),
    calls mult_mod and mult_vec, and finally prints a 64–bit result.
*/
main:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Allocate a 2592-byte block with calloc.
		mov		w0, #1
		mov		w1, #2592
		bl		calloc
		mov		x19, x0

		// For demonstration, load a “one” vector and then store it into two chosen offsets.
		adr		x0, one_const
		ptrue	p0.d
		ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x0]
		// Compute address for offset 144
		add		x9, x19, #144
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x9]
		// Compute address for offset 1432
		add		x9, x19, #1432
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x9]

		// Call mult_mod (both parameters = pointer in x19).
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_mod

		// Then call mult_vec.
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_vec

		// Load a 64–bit result from offset 64 and print it via printf.
		ldr		x8, [x0, #64]
		adr		x0, fmt_str
		mov		x1, x8
		bl		printf

		mov		w0, wzr
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
		ret

	.data
	.align	3
// A full 64–bit constant (repeated to form a vector).
mod_const:
		.dword	0x000000003B3ACA00
// A reciprocal constant for mod reduction.
recip_const:
		.dword	0x000000000002D79C
// Coefficient constant (the value 2)
coeff_const:
		.dword	0x0000000000000002
// A zero vector (with at least 4 dwords).
zero_const:
		.dword	0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0
// A “one” vector.
one_const:
		.dword	0x1, 0x1, 0x1, 0x1
// Format string for printf.
fmt_str:
		.asciz	"%llu\n"
	.text

.arch armv8.2-a+sve
	.align 3
	.text
	.global mult_mod
	.type	mult_mod, %function
/*  
  Function: mult_mod 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (for example, to an input “array”)
    x1 = an extra parameter (unused in this example)
  Operation:
    Allocates 2592 bytes via malloc; then using SVE it “processes” the input data in vector chunks.
    In each chunk it:
      • loads a vector of 64‐bit elements (ld1d with p0/z),
      • shifts left and right (lsl/lsr using p0/m),
      • masks with a 32–bit immediate (and without a predicate),
      • does a multiply–add (mla indexed using p0/m – note the use of “[0]” to select lane 0),
      • then does the “mod reduction” (umulh plus mls using p0/m)
    and finally writes the answer (st1d).
*/
mult_mod:
		// Prologue: save frame pointer and link register.
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Save parameters: x0 -> x19 and x1 -> x20.
		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 2592 bytes via malloc.
		mov		w0, #2592
		// Set up the “mod constant” in w21: first lower then upper half.
		mov		w21, #51712		        // 0xCA00
		movk		w21, #15258, lsl #16		// => 0x3B3ACA00
		bl		malloc		           
		mov		x24, x0			// x24 = allocated pointer

		// Initialize loop counter.
		mov		x8, #0

		// Set up predicate for all 64–bit (doubleword) elements.
		ptrue	p0.d

		// Get the current vector length multiplied by 8.
		rdvl	x10, #8
		// Compute the number of 64–bit elements in the predicate: each element is 8 bytes.
		lsr		x11, x10, #3

		// Load the mod constant and its reciprocal as a “vector constant”.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z1 = mod constant (0x3B3ACA00)

		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z2 = reciprocal constant

		// Load a coefficient constant (for multiplying data) from memory.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// e.g. constant 2

mult_mod_loop:
		cmp		x8, #2592
		b.ge		mult_mod_exit

		// Load one vector (64–bit elements) from [x19, x8, lsl #3].
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0/z, [x19, x8, lsl #3]

		// Shift left then right using the predicate in merge mode.
		lsl		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #1
		lsr		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #1

		// Mask each element to 32–bits; note no predicate is used.
		and		z4.d, z4.d, #0xFFFFFFFF

		// Zero an accumulator vector by loading our zero constant.
		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate (z4 * constant) into z5.
		mla		z5.d, p0/m, z4.d, z3.d[0]

		// Do mod reduction:
		//     result = original_z5 - ( high(original_z5*z2) * z1 )
		mov		z7.d, z5.d
		umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, z2.d
		mls		z5.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

		// Store the result vector into the allocated block.
		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		// Increment our element–offset by the number of active elements.
		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_mod_loop

mult_mod_exit:
		mov		x0, x24
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #96
		ret

	.global mult_vec
	.type	mult_vec, %function
/*
  Function: mult_vec 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (to an input data block)
    x1 = pointer (to accessing a coefficient array)
  Operation:
    Allocates 144 bytes via malloc and then processes data in an SVE loop.
    (It loads data, shifts and masks with immediate constants, does an mla (with the index [0])
    and mod reduction via umulh and mls.)
*/
mult_vec:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-80]!
		mov		x29, sp

		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 144 bytes.
		mov		w0, #144
		mov		w21, #51712
		movk	w21, #15258, lsl #16
		bl		malloc
		mov		x24, x0

		ptrue	p0.d
		rdvl	x10, #8
		lsr		x11, x10, #3

		// Load coefficient constant.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		mov		x8, #0
mult_vec_loop:
		cmp		x8, #144
		b.ge		mult_vec_exit

		// Load one vector from [x20, x8, lsl #3].
		ld1d	{ z4.d }, p0/z, [x20, x8, lsl #3]

		// Shift left then right (using immediate #2).
		lsl		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #2
		lsr		z4.d, p0/m, z4.d, #2

		// Mask each element to 16–bits.
		and		z4.d, z4.d, #0xFFFF

		adr		x0, zero_const
		ld1d	{ z5.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Multiply–add: accumulate (z4 * constant) into z5.
		mla		z5.d, p0/m, z4.d, z3.d[0]

		// For mod–reduction, load the mod constant and its reciprocal.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0/z, [x0]
		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0/z, [x0]

		// Copy z5 into a temporary, then do mod reduction.
		mov		z7.d, z5.d
		umulh	z7.d, p0/m, z7.d, z2.d
		mls		z5.d, p0/m, z7.d, z1.d

		st1d	{ z5.d }, p0, [x24, x8, lsl #3]

		add		x8, x8, x11
		b		mult_vec_loop

mult_vec_exit:
		mov		x0, x24
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #80
		ret

	.global main
	.type	main, %function
/*
  Function: main
  Operation:
    Allocates a 2592–byte block with calloc, then (for demo)
    stores the “one” constant at two chosen offsets,
    calls mult_mod and mult_vec, and finally prints a 64–bit result.
*/
main:
		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-64]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Allocate a 2592–byte block with calloc.
		mov		w0, #1
		mov		w1, #2592
		bl		calloc
		mov		x19, x0

		// For demonstration, load a “one” vector and then store it into two offsets.
		adr		x0, one_const
		ptrue	p0.d
		ld1d	{ z0.d }, p0/z, [x0]
		// Compute address for offset 144
		add		x9, x19, #144
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x9]
		// Compute address for offset 1432
		add		x9, x19, #1432
		st1d	{ z0.d }, p0, [x9]

		// Call mult_mod (both parameters = pointer in x19).
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_mod

		// Then call mult_vec.
		mov		x0, x19
		mov		x1, x19
		bl		mult_vec

		// Load a 64–bit result from offset 64 and print it via printf.
		ldr		x8, [x0, #64]
		adr		x0, fmt_str
		mov		x1, x8
		bl		printf

		mov		w0, wzr
		ldp		x29, x30, [sp], #64
		ret

	.data
	.align	3
// A full 64–bit constant (repeated to form a vector).
mod_const:
		.dword	0x000000003B3ACA00
// A reciprocal constant for mod reduction.
recip_const:
		.dword	0x000000000002D79C
// Coefficient constant (the value 2)
coeff_const:
		.dword	0x0000000000000002
// A zero vector (with at least 4 dwords).
zero_const:
		.dword	0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0
// A “one” vector.
one_const:
		.dword	0x1, 0x1, 0x1, 0x1
// Format string for printf.
fmt_str:
		.asciz	"%llu\n"
	.text

  Function: mult_mod 
  Input:
    x0 = pointer (for example, to an input “array”)
    x1 = an extra parameter (unused in this example)

      • shifts left and right (lsl/lsr using p0/m),
      • masks with a 32–bit immediate (and without a predicate),
      • does a multiply–add (mla indexed using p0/m – note the implicit lane #0 given via “, #0”),
      • then does the “mod reduction” (umulh plus mls using p0/m)

*/
mult_mod:

		stp		x29, x30, [sp, #-96]!
		mov		x29, sp

		// Save parameters: x0 -> x19 and x1 -> x20.
		mov		x19, x0
		mov		x20, x1

		// Allocate 2592 bytes via malloc.
		mov		w0, #2592
		// Set up the “mod constant” in w21: first lower then upper half.
		mov		w21, #51712		        // 0xCA00
		movk		w21, #15258, lsl #16		// => 0x3B3ACA00

		mov		x24, x0			// x24 = allocated pointer

		// Initialize loop counter.
		mov		x8, #0

		// Set up predicate for all 64–bit (doubleword) elements.
		ptrue	p0.d

		// Get the current vector length multiplied by 8.
		rdvl	x10, #8
		// Compute the number of 64–bit elements in the predicate: each element is 8 bytes.
		lsr		x11, x10, #3

		// Load the mod constant and its reciprocal as a “vector constant”.
		adr		x0, mod_const
		ld1d	{ z1.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z1 = mod constant (0x3B3ACA00)

		adr		x0, recip_const
		ld1d	{ z2.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// z2 = reciprocal constant

		// Load a coefficient constant (for multiplying data) from memory.
		adr		x0, coeff_const
		ld1d	{ z3.d }, p0/z, [x0]		// e.g. constant 2

		cmp		x8, #2592
